# Onboarding science and enterprise setup patterns: research notes for Metis

Research date: 2026-10-02. Purpose: evidence base for the Metis onboarding brainstorm and requirements document (target: any customer sets up its company workspace in 30 minutes, without slide tours and without long wizards). An external reviewer will fact-check this file, so every claim carries a URL and a date.

## How to read this file

- Citations: for web sources the citation is the URL plus the publication or update date shown on the page; where a page shows no date, the access date 2026-10-02 is given.
- Verification status, used in every section (each section keeps the labels its researcher used; they map as follows):
  - Primary, opened: P (section 1), FETCHED (section 2), fetched (section 3), see section 4 legend, [F] (sections 5 and 6). The claim was read on the cited page, or in the paper's abstract retrieved from the publisher, Crossref or Semantic Scholar.
  - Secondary, opened: S (section 1). Read on a secondary page (for example Wikipedia or an NN/g summary) that cites the original.
  - Not confirmed: [Unverified - confirm before applying] (also written U, SEARCH ONLY, search summary only, or [S]). Seen only in a search-engine summary or on a page that could not be opened. Do not apply these without checking.
- Vendor numbers without a stated method are labelled "vendor claim, method not stated". They indicate what vendors promise, not what customers get.
- Method limit: the session-wide web search budget (200 searches) ran out part-way through the work. Later checks used direct page fetches on known URLs only. Items that could not be confirmed this way stay marked unverified; nothing was filled in from memory.
- Spot checks by the lead researcher after the topic notes were written (all re-opened on 2026-10-02 and confirmed): WorkOS portal link intents, 5-minute expiry and 20-email limit; Microsoft Entra gallery SCIM requirement of at least 100 mutual customers and 25 requests per second; Workday GO "as few as 60 business days"; Drata time to value 144 to 66 days (Gainsight Pulse 2026); HubSpot import rollback within 14 days; Microsoft message MC1478955 (Project Online retires 30 Sep 2026).

## Key findings in one page

1. The behavioural levers with the best evidence for setup are defaults (meta-analysis) and progress framing (field experiments). Defaults shift choices with d = 0.68 across 58 studies; fewer than 5% of users in one practitioner study had changed any setting; a loyalty card that started with 2 of 10 stamps filled was redeemed by 34% of customers versus 19% for an empty 8-stamp card. The Zeigarnik "open loop" memory effect does not replicate (ratio 0.99), but interrupted tasks are resumed 67% of the time, so resumable setup matters more than nagging.
2. Length hurts, but what counts differs by format. For forms, the number of fields, especially free-text and drop-down inputs, matters more than the number of screens (Baymard, HubSpot). For guided tours, completion falls steeply with each step: three-step tours complete at 72% versus 16% for seven steps. Onboarding checklists complete at a median of 10.1%, and slide-style tutorials did not improve task performance in NN/g testing. User-started guidance completes far more often than guidance the product launches.
3. In enterprise B2B, the slow parts of setup sit with other people: IT (SSO, SCIM, DNS, which can take up to 72 hours), finance, approvers and data owners. Leading products hand these to the owner through scoped links, approved-domain self-join, nominate and auto-approve cycles, and ask-the-owner requests.
4. Existing data is the fastest route to value and the riskiest step. Good importers layer exact, fuzzy, historical and AI column mapping behind a confidence gate, validate without writing, report what was kept and dropped, land in a draft or scenario, and can undo an import. Microsoft Project Online retired on 30 Sep 2026, so many PMOs now hold their plans in .mpp, MSPDI XML and Excel.
5. Enterprise vendors sell speed as preconfigured, fixed-scope packages (Workday GO, NetSuite SuiteSuccess, Planview planning package, a ServiceNow SPM partner pack) measured in weeks or months, not minutes. The most transferable mechanism is Workday Launch: a preconfigured tenant preloaded with the customer's own data, reviewed against the standard. No verified vendor offers a literal implementation in a day for governance or PPM software.
6. Configuration packs only scale if changes are safe: packages are immutable versions (Salesforce), changes are previewed as a diff with typed problems before commit (ServiceNow update sets, Terraform plan), and rollouts are previewed on a copy of one real project (Smartsheet). Back-out is the least reliable step even on mature platforms, so fix-forward with new versions is preferred.
7. After go-live, configuration can keep improving from the tenant's own data: daily computed recommendations (Microsoft Entra), ranked actions with honest closing states (Secure Score), starter suggestions while the account is sparse (Datadog) and suggestions inferred from content (GitHub, Asana, Linear).

| P39 | Labelled sample data that an admin removes in one action | Pipedrive | https://support.pipedrive.com/en/article/sample-data (3 Sep 2026) | LRN |
| P40 | Fixed-scope preconfigured package, phased "stairway" | Workday GO; NetSuite SuiteSuccess; Planview planning package; Capture SmartStart | URLs in E29 and E30 | CFG, LRN |
| P41 | Vendor-led onboarding with a pilot group and a named specialist | Ramp; HubSpot required onboarding | https://ramp.com/versus/concur (accessed 2026-10-02); https://www.hubspot.com/services/onboarding/advanced-and-premier (accessed 2026-10-02) | DATA, LRN |


## C. The six most transferable ideas for Metis

Framing that follows from the evidence: in this research, no verified enterprise vendor sets up governance or PPM software in minutes (E29, E30, E33). The 30-minute goal is therefore best defined as "a published, usable workspace on recommended defaults, holding the customer's real project list". The slow, external steps (IT, DNS, approvers, finance, data owners) run in parallel and finish after the session.

1. **Start from a recommended governance pack, edit it as a draft, publish through a plan preview.** No blank workspace and no long wizard. Offer one recommended pack per industry or team type, with at most two or three alternatives. A first-time admin choosing a governance framework faces every condition under which choice overload appears (E8). Defaults are sticky and work best when they signal endorsement (E5 to E7). Let the admin make a few visible edits (stage names, gate approvers, quorum), because ownership grows only when the work is finished (E4). Edit the framework on one canvas with live checks: NN/g advises against wizards when steps depend on each other (section 5.4.3). Publish through a plan that shows what will be created, changed or removed, with typed problems that must each get a decision (P19, P20, P28). Packs are immutable, numbered versions; a version 2 rollout is previewed on a copy of one real project first, and fixes go forward as new versions rather than back-outs (P18, P25, E35, E36). Bottlenecks: configuration, learning.

2. **Load the customer's own data in the first minutes with a "bring your plan" importer.** Accept .mpp and MSPDI XML, Excel and CSV, plus Smartsheet, Jira, monday and Asana exports (E24, P14). Map columns in layers (exact match, synonyms, tenant history, then AI) behind a confidence gate, and visibly mark what the AI chose (P11, P12). Ask one structural question to build the portfolio, program, project and WBS tree. Map resource names to people, or to placeholders that bind when the person joins (P16). Before anything is written: validate, then show what will be kept, changed and dropped (P13, P14, P15). The import lands in a draft or scenario, carries a batch id and can be undone for a fixed window (P17, E26). Review configuration on the customer's data, not dummy data (P27, E33). Bottlenecks: existing data, people and access.

3. **Take identity and access off the 30-minute path.** The first admin starts on password plus MFA. SSO, SCIM, domain verification and group-to-role mapping go to IT as scoped links that expire and close themselves when done (P1, P2, E21). DNS verification can take up to 72 hours, so it runs in the background (E20). An approved company domain with a default role lets colleagues join on their own, with just-in-time accounts at first SSO sign-in and invites limited to the inviter's own role (P4 to P6). Okta and Entra catalog listings come later; Entra's SCIM listing needs 100 shared customers first (P3, E22). Bottleneck: people and access.

4. **Send the remaining decisions to their owners as pre-filled micro-tasks that auto-accept.** Finance confirms currency, fiscal calendar and budget categories. Each gate's approvers confirm membership and quorum. The PMO lead confirms the lifecycle, and project managers complete charters. Each task has a soft deadline and an automatic acceptance date (P8), the coordinator tracks progress by assignee (P7) and owners enter their own data before review (P9). Anyone blocked uses an "ask the owner" request that carries its context (P10). Ask each owner for a specific time to do the task, since if-then plans raise follow-through (E9). Collect the few irreversible settings first, from the right person: fiscal calendar type, base currency once budgets exist (P21, section 5.3.3). Invite people into a job rather than counting invites: team accounts retain better, but invites alone were not predictive (E23). Bottlenecks: configuration, people and access.

5. **Replace tours with a short, honest, resumable setup list that starts part-done, and with help in context.** Pre-complete the items that sign-up and defaults already cover, and say why (E1; the paper found that a stated reason moderates the effect). Show progress as a share of a short list, keep any guided run to about three steps, and show a progress bar only when early progress looks fast (E2, E10, E14). Save everything and reopen where the user stopped: interrupted tasks are resumed, while "open loop" memory effects do not replicate (E3). Prefer help the user opens over tours the product launches, teach through empty states, and state the true time up front (E11, E15, E16, P38). Cut free-text and drop-down inputs, since the number of fields matters more than the number of screens (E12, E13). Do not rely on the checklist alone: the median completion rate is 10.1% (E17). Bottleneck: learning.

6. **After go-live, keep configuring from observed usage, and coach the first governance cycle.** Run a daily workspace health check that lists only the items that apply and routes each to its owning role (P30). Rank actions and allow honest closing states such as "risk accepted" or "resolved through third party", as Secure Score does (P31). Show starter suggestions only while the workspace is sparse (P32), and infer option lists or frameworks from imported data (P33). Ask for an integration the first time it is needed (P35, P37). Defer only settings that can be changed later (P36). Pair this with a person who coaches the customer through the first real gate review, as Planview's packages include. The only outcome evidence is a single-company before-and-after (E27) plus correlational survey data (E28). Bottlenecks: configuration, learning.

## D. Gaps, NOT RUN items and claims to confirm before use

Evidence gaps (searched for, not found):
- No controlled, public study isolates the effect of templates or sample data on B2B activation (section 1.12; section 4.8).
- No independent study measures AI column-mapping accuracy or the time it saves; every number is a vendor claim (section 3.1).
- No source measures how much a delegated IT setup link shortens SSO setup (section 2.9).
- No method-stated benchmark of time to value for sales-led enterprise implementations; Userpilot's figures describe product-led first value events (section 1.11).
- No verified vendor offers a literal "implementation in a day" for governance or PPM software (section 6).

NOT RUN (with reason): Workday onboarding task routing (search budget exhausted, docs behind login); Planview and other PPM accelerator packs beyond the Planview planning package page (search budget exhausted); Atlassian Terraform provider, Jira and Linear workflow export (search budget exhausted, URLs tried returned 404); monday.com managed templates (HTTP 403). Details in sections 2.9 and 4.9.

Claims marked [Unverified - confirm before applying] in the sections, to check before any requirement relies on them: the 300-card sample size in Nunes and Dreze (1.1); Madrian and Shea participation percentages (1.5); the Airtable template experiment and the Chameleon demo activation figure (1.12); Miro domain control (2.3); the original Microsoft Planner blog post on the Project Online retirement, the Planner Power App list of unsupported features, Osmos product sunset, ClickUp importer limits, Planview AdaptiveWork validation report, monday.com lack of native .mpp import (3.0 to 3.4); Salesforce InstallHandler, ServiceNow Store dependency checklist, NetSuite "100 days or less", SAP "228 scopes" (4.1 to 4.5); Entra 90-day threshold, Okta HealthInsight tabs, Datadog 2020 blog details, Linear guidance, Salesforce Optimizer retirement, Vercel detection, NetSuite India page, PPM Pro FastTrack packages, Meisterplan G2 quotes, Smartsheet Accelerators, HubSpot Sales and Service Hub fees, monday.com hour packages, Rippling and Gusto services, ServiceNow phase names (sections 5 and 6).

# Detailed notes by topic

Each section below was researched separately and keeps its own status labels (mapped in "How to read this file" above).


## 1. Behavioural evidence and onboarding benchmarks

Access date for every web source in this section: 2026-10-02 unless a publication date is given.
Verification key: **P** = primary source opened (paper full text, abstract via publisher or Crossref or Semantic Scholar, or the vendor's own report page or PDF); **S** = secondary source opened (Wikipedia, NN/g summary, trade press); **U** = [Unverified - confirm before applying].

### 1.1 Endowed progress effect (Nunes and Dreze 2006)

- Citation: Nunes, J. C. and Dreze, X. (2006). The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort. Journal of Consumer Research 32(4), 504 to 512, published 1 March 2006. DOI https://doi.org/10.1086/500480. Abstract page: https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-lookup/doi/10.1086/500480 (P, abstract only).
- Abstract (P): people given artificial advancement toward a goal persist more. Turning an 8-step task into a 10-step task with 2 steps already done raised the likelihood of completion and cut completion time. The effect works through perceived progress, not through reluctance to waste the free head start. Moderators: whether the endowment is justified (a reason is given) and the unit in which progress is recorded.
- Field numbers (S, Wikipedia "Goal pursuit", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_pursuit, citing the paper): car wash loyalty cards; endowed cards (10 stamps needed, 2 pre-stamped) redeemed at 34% versus 19% for unendowed cards (8 stamps needed). 300 cards distributed (S, same page; full text not opened, so treat the 300 figure as U until the paper is checked). Full-text PDF copies tried and failed: USC copy (404), publisher PDF (403), psicologo-milano.it copy (403).
- Quality: peer-reviewed field experiment plus lab studies; a single site; the 34% versus 19% figure is the best known number but was confirmed only through a secondary source in this session.
- Metis transfer: start the setup checklist with items already done by sign-up and by smart defaults (tenant created, domain detected, default calendars, a recommended framework installed) and give a reason for the head start ("we pre-filled these from your sign-up"), because the paper found justification moderates the effect.

### 1.2 Goal-gradient effect (Kivetz, Urminsky and Zheng 2006)

- Citation: Kivetz, R., Urminsky, O. and Zheng, Y. (2006). The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected: Purchase Acceleration, Illusionary Goal Progress, and Customer Retention. Journal of Marketing Research 43(1), 39 to 58. DOI 10.1509/jmkr.43.1.39. Author manuscript opened: https://www.columbia.edu/~rk566/Session4/Goal-Gradient_Illusionary_Goal_Progress.pdf (P, full text).
- Cafe reward programme ("buy ten coffees, get one free"): 949 completed cards, nearly ten thousand purchases. Inter-purchase times fall by 20% (0.7 days) from the first to the last purchase on a card (manuscript p. 3 and p. 10 to 11).
- Illusionary progress field experiment, N = 108 cafe customers randomly given a 10-stamp card or a 12-stamp card with 2 "bonus" stamps: the 10 required purchases took 15.6 days (control) versus 12.7 days (bonus stamps), about 20% faster; medians 15 versus 10 days (Mann-Whitney p < .05) (manuscript p. 21 to 22).
- Also found: effort depends on the proportion of distance remaining, not the absolute distance; people slow down right after a reward ("post-reward resetting"); steeper acceleration toward the first reward predicts retention and faster re-engagement.
- Quality: peer-reviewed; field experiments, secondary customer data and hazard models; consumer reward context.
- Metis transfer: show progress as a proportion of a short list (for example "5 of 7 to go live") and put the quickest items last as well as first so the end of setup accelerates; expect a lull after "workspace published" and plan the next goal (first gate review) immediately.

### 1.3 Zeigarnik and Ovsiankina effects (2025 meta-analysis)

- Citation: Ghibellini, R. and Meier, B. (2025). Interruption, recall and resumption: a meta-analysis of the Zeigarnik and Ovsiankina effects. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 12:962, published 1 July 2025. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41599-025-05000-w (P, full text opened; abstract also confirmed via Crossref).
- Method: 1,455 records screened, 59 publications included (38 Zeigarnik, 20 Ovsiankina, 1 both).
- Zeigarnik (memory for unfinished tasks): weighted ratio of recalled interrupted to recalled completed tasks = 0.99 (38 publications), that is, no memory advantage; percentage measure 49.43% (14 publications), a slight disadvantage.
- Ovsiankina (tendency to resume interrupted tasks): weighted resumption rate 67.00% (21 publications) against a 50% chance level.
- Authors' conclusion: "the Ovsiankina effect represents a general tendency, whereas the Zeigarnik effect lacks universal validity."
- Quality: meta-analysis, high; note that most included studies are old laboratory studies.
- Metis transfer: do not rely on "open loops" to make admins remember setup; rely on resumption instead: save every partial step, reopen exactly where the user stopped, and show the one next action. Nagging badges are not supported by this evidence; a visible "resume" entry point is.

### 1.4 IKEA effect (Norton, Mochon and Ariely 2012; meta-analysis 2025)

- Original: Norton, M. I., Mochon, D. and Ariely, D. (2012). The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love. Journal of Consumer Psychology 22, 453 to 460 (online 9 Sep 2011). DOI 10.1016/j.jcps.2011.08.002 (P, abstract via Crossref and Semantic Scholar).
  - Four studies (IKEA boxes, origami, Lego). Self-made products were valued more; participants saw their amateur creations as similar in value to experts' creations.
  - Boundary: "labor leads to love only when labor results in successful completion of tasks"; building then destroying, or failing to complete, removed the effect.
- Meta-analysis: Pelled, A., Demetriades, S. Z. and Walter, N. Labor Leads to Love, Right? A Meta-Analysis of the IKEA Effect. Psychology and Marketing, online 14 Oct 2025 (issue 43(2), 2026). DOI 10.1002/mar.70064 (P, abstract via Crossref).
  - k = 55, N = 5,454; d = 0.57 (p < 0.005) on valuation; also raises liking, self-concept and sense of ownership; robust across moderators such as customization and tangibility.
- Quality: high (meta-analysis), but consumer products, not software configuration.
- Metis transfer: let the customer make a few visible, meaningful edits to a pre-built framework (rename stages, choose gate approvers, set quorum) so they own it, and make sure each edit ends in a completed, published artefact; unfinished effort earns no ownership.

### 1.5 Default effects and choice architecture

- Meta-analysis: Jachimowicz, J. M., Duncan, S., Weber, E. U. and Johnson, E. J. (2019). When and why defaults influence decisions: a meta-analysis of default effects. Behavioural Public Policy 3(2), 159 to 186 (online 24 Jan 2019). DOI 10.1017/bpp.2018.43 (P, abstract via Crossref; also https://collaborate.princeton.edu/en/publications/when-and-why-defaults-influence-decisions-a-meta-analysis-of-defa/).
  - 58 studies, pooled n = 73,675; d = 0.68 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.83). Most studies positive, several null, two negative.
  - Moderators: stronger in consumer domains, weaker in environmental domains; stronger when the default conveys endorsement (what the designer recommends) or endowment (the status quo).
- Smart defaults: Smith, N. C., Goldstein, D. G. and Johnson, E. J. (2013). Choice without Awareness: Ethical and Policy Implications of Defaults. Journal of Public Policy and Marketing 32, 159 to 172. DOI 10.1509/jppm.10.114 (P, abstract via Crossref). Three causes of default effects: implied endorsement, cognitive biases, effort. Proposes "smart defaults"; notes active choice is not always better when preferences are not established.
- Retirement saving: Madrian, B. C. and Shea, D. F. (2001). The Power of Suggestion: Inertia in 401(k) Participation and Savings Behavior. Quarterly Journal of Economics. NBER working paper page https://www.nber.org/papers/w7682 (P, abstract): participation "significantly higher under automatic enrollment"; a substantial fraction of auto-enrolled participants keep both the default contribution rate and the default fund. Specific participation percentages not confirmed in this session (U).
- Software settings: Spool, J. (14 Sep 2011). Do users change their settings? UIE Brainsparks. https://archive.uie.com/brainsparks/2011/09/14/do-users-change-their-settings/ (S/P, practitioner study): several hundred people sent their Microsoft Word settings files; 150+ settings; "Less than 5% of the users we surveyed had changed any settings at all." Quality: self-selected sample, not peer-reviewed.
- Pendo (2019). The 2019 Feature Adoption Report. https://www.pendo.io/resources/the-2019-feature-adoption-report/ (P): 615 Pendo subscriptions (customers using Pendo for more than a year), three months of usage: an average of 12% of features generate 80% of daily usage volume; 80% of features are rarely or never used. Quality: vendor data, Pendo customers only; "feature" means a tagged UI element.
- Metis transfer: ship an opinionated, endorsed default for every setting (calendar, currency from domain or locale, reporting cadence, option lists, a stage-gate framework) and label it "recommended for organisations like yours"; most settings will never be revisited, so the default is the configuration for most tenants. Keep active choice only where there is no safe default (who approves gates).

### 1.6 Choice overload (when many options hurt)

- Scheibehenne, B., Greifeneder, R. and Todd, P. M. (2010). Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload. Journal of Consumer Research 37, 409 to 425 (P, abstract via OUP page https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-lookup/doi/10.1086/651235): 63 conditions from 50 experiments, N = 5,036; mean effect "virtually zero" with considerable variance.
- Chernev, A., Bockenholt, U. and Goodman, J. (2015). Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis. Journal of Consumer Psychology 25, 333 to 358 (online 29 Aug 2014). DOI 10.1016/j.jcps.2014.08.002 (P, abstract via Crossref): 99 observations, N = 7,202; overload is reliable when choice sets are complex, the task is difficult, preferences are uncertain and the person wants to minimise effort.
- Metis transfer: a first-time admin choosing a governance framework matches all four overload conditions, so the setup should present one recommended framework plus at most two or three alternatives, not a gallery of dozens.

### 1.7 Implementation intentions (for distributed setup tasks)

- Gollwitzer, P. M. and Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 38, 69 to 119. DOI 10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1 (P, abstract via Semantic Scholar): 94 independent tests; if-then plans that specify when, where and how had a medium-to-large effect on goal attainment (d = .65).
- Metis transfer: when the admin delegates a task (finance sets currency and budget categories, PMO lead reviews the framework), ask the assignee to pick a specific slot or trigger ("when I open the review link on Tuesday") and deliver the task inside that context.

### 1.8 Progress indicators

- Villar, A., Callegaro, M. and Yang, Y. (2013). Where Am I? A Meta-Analysis of Experiments on the Effects of Progress Indicators for Web Surveys. Social Science Computer Review (online 19 Aug 2013). DOI 10.1177/0894439313497468 (P, abstract via Crossref): 32 randomized experiments. A constant-speed progress indicator did not significantly reduce drop-off; fast-to-slow indicators reduced drop-off; slow-to-fast indicators increased drop-off; with a small promised incentive, a constant indicator increased drop-off.
- Conrad, F. G., Couper, M. P., Tourangeau, R. and Peytchev, A. (2010). The impact of progress indicators on task completion. Interacting with Computers 22. DOI 10.1016/j.intcom.2010.03.001 (P, abstract via Semantic Scholar): two experiments; when early feedback showed slow progress, abandonment was higher; intermittent feedback reduced the cost of discouraging feedback.
- Chameleon (2019). Product Tour Benchmarks and Best Practices. https://www.chameleon.io/assets/chameleon-product-tour-benchmarks-report-2019.pdf (P, vendor PDF): progress indicators improved tour completion by 12% and cut dismissal by 20% (15 million tour interactions; vendor data, method partly stated).
- Metis transfer: show a progress meter only if early progress looks fast (pre-completed and one-click items first); never show a bar that starts slow, for example "step 1 of 14".

### 1.9 Length, steps and fields versus completion

- Galesic, M. and Bosnjak, M. (2009). Effects of Questionnaire Length on Participation and Indicators of Response Quality in a Web Survey. Public Opinion Quarterly 73(2), 349 to 360, published 28 May 2009 (P, abstract https://academic.oup.com/poq/article-abstract/73/2/349/1939196): stated lengths of 10, 20 and 30 minutes; "the longer the stated length, the fewer respondents started and completed the questionnaire"; later questions got faster, shorter and more uniform answers. (Exact start rates per group seen only in secondary summaries: U.)
- Baymard Institute (26 Jun 2024). Checkout Optimization: Minimize Form Fields. https://baymard.com/blog/checkout-flow-average-form-fields (P): the average checkout in 2024 has 11.3 form fields while 8 are enough; 17% of users abandoned because of checkout complexity (Baymard 2024 survey of US adults); "the number of form fields in a checkout impacts overall usability far more than the number of steps."
- HubSpot, Dan Zarrella. Which Types of Form Fields Lower Landing Page Conversions? https://blog.hubspot.com/blog/tabid/6307/bid/6746/which-types-of-form-fields-lower-landing-page-conversions.aspx (P, page updated 6 Jun 2025): over 40,000 HubSpot customer landing pages; "as the number of form fields increases, conversion rates decrease slightly, but not as steeply as I expected"; single-line text fields cost little, while multiple text areas and multiple drop-downs have "a powerful depressing effect". Quality: observational, not controlled; old data.
- Expedia optional "Company" field (anecdote): removing it yielded "$12m of profit a year" (Expedia's Joe Megibow to Silicon.com), reported by UsabilityCounts, 29 Nov 2010, https://www.usabilitycounts.com/2010/11/29/silicon-com-expedia-on-how-one-extra-data-field-can-cost-12-million/ (S). Quality: executive anecdote, no method.
- Chameleon (2022 Benchmark Report). https://www.chameleon.io/benchmark-report-2022 (P, vendor page): 300 million end-user interactions (58 million tours in the last 12 months): tours with 3 steps had a 72% completion rate, and only 16% of tours with 7 steps were completed (paraphrase of the page).
- Chameleon (2019) PDF above (P): 15 million interactions; average tour completion 61%; 4-step tours 46% versus 5-step tours 23%; tours the user starts (self-serve) had 123% higher completion than tours the product launched automatically; tours triggered from a checklist were 21% more likely to be completed and about 60% of users went on to complete a second tour.
- NN/g, Raluca Budiu (25 Jun 2017). Wizards: Definition and Design Recommendations. https://www.nngroup.com/articles/wizards/ (S, expert guidance): wizards suit novices and infrequent processes such as configuration or setup; drawbacks include interaction cost, poor recoverability if interrupted and blocking other areas; recommendations include a visible step list, save and resume, and reusing previous selections as defaults.
- Metis transfer: the cost driver is the number of decisions and free-text or drop-down inputs, not the number of screens; cut inputs through defaults and inference, keep any guided sequence to about three steps, and make every step resumable.

### 1.10 Tours, tutorials and learning by doing

- NN/g, Alita Kendrick (21 Jun 2020). Mobile-App Onboarding: An Analysis of Components and Techniques. https://www.nngroup.com/articles/mobile-app-onboarding/ (S): NN/g testing found deck-of-cards "tutorials didn't improve task performance"; recommends contextual help, a visible Skip, and onboarding that is "brief, optional" and shows only the minimum.
- NN/g, Jakob Nielsen (4 Oct 1998). Paradox of the Active User. https://www.nngroup.com/articles/paradox-of-the-active-user/ (S): from Carroll and Rosson's IBM studies, "Users never read manuals but start using the software immediately."
- Atkinson, R. K., Derry, S. J., Renkl, A. and Wortham, D. (2000). Learning from Examples: Instructional Principles from the Worked Examples Research. Review of Educational Research 70, 181 to 214. DOI 10.3102/00346543070002181 (P, abstract via Crossref): worked examples (an expert's solution to study) are associated with early skill development; examples should sit next to matched practice. Theoretical support for templates and sample frameworks as worked examples.
- Metis transfer: replace slide tours with user-triggered, in-context help and with a worked example (a sample portfolio or a completed sample gate) that sits next to the real task.

### 1.11 SaaS onboarding benchmarks (vendor and practitioner data)

- Userpilot, SaaS Product Metrics Benchmark Report (page labelled 2025, figures from the 2024 report). https://userpilot.com/saas-product-metrics/ (P, vendor page); 2024 summary https://userpilot.com/blog/product-metrics-benchmark-report/ (P, last updated 7 Apr 2026; 547 companies across the whole report):
  - User activation rate: average 37.5%, median 37.04% (62 companies; Userpilot activation dashboard).
  - Time to value: average 1 day 12 hours 23 minutes (62 companies; user activation dashboard). SLG 1 day 11 hours versus PLG 1 day 12 hours.
  - Onboarding checklist completion: average 19.2%, median 10.1% (188 companies).
  - Core feature adoption: average 24.5%, median 16.5% (181 companies).
  - 1-month retention: average 46.9%, median 45.25% (83 companies).
  - Quality: vendor customer data, each company defines its own activation and value event, selection bias toward Userpilot customers; useful as a rough order of magnitude only.
- Lenny Rachitsky and Yuriy Timen (25 Oct 2022). What is a good activation rate. https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/what-is-a-good-activation-rate (P): more than 500 survey responses; average activation 34%, median 25%; SaaS only average 36%, median 30%; about 6% of respondents used time-bound definitions (median window 10 days, mode 7). Activation milestone defined by each respondent as predictive of retention (at least 2x). Quality: self-reported survey.
- Wyzowl (2020). Customer Onboarding Statistics 2020, one-page PDF https://wyzowl.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/pdfs/Wyzowl-onboarding-stats-one-pager.pdf (P); web page https://wyzowl.com/customer-onboarding-statistics/ (blocked 403 in this session): 216 people surveyed in early 2020; 88% (PDF; secondary sources quote 86% from the web page) more likely to stay loyal to a business that invests in onboarding content; 63% say onboarding matters to the purchase decision; 8 in 10 deleted an app because they did not know how to use it; 55% returned a product they did not understand. Quality: small consumer survey by a video agency; low relevance to enterprise B2B.
- No primary, method-stated benchmark for enterprise (sales-led, multi-week implementation) time to value was found in this section; Userpilot's figure describes product-led first value events, not an enterprise go-live.

### 1.12 Templates and sample data versus activation

- No controlled, public study with a stated method was found that isolates the effect of templates or sample data on B2B activation.
- Reported but not confirmed in this session: an Airtable onboarding experiment (Reforge write-up by a former Airtable growth lead) in which personalised templates raised onboarding completion about 15% but reduced sharing about 10% [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Reported but not confirmed: Chameleon users who engaged with an interactive demo activated at 50.85% versus 41.2% [Unverified - confirm before applying; self-selected comparison].
- Supporting theory: worked-examples research (1.10) and default effects (1.5).
- Metis transfer: treat templates as a hypothesis to test inside Metis (randomise by tenant, count activation only on the customer's own data) rather than as proven; watch for templates lowering collaboration, as the unconfirmed Airtable result suggests.


## 2. Delegated and distributed setup

Scope: how B2B products move setup work off the first admin and onto the people who own each piece (customer IT, domain owners, managers, employees), and how they let people join or ask for access without an admin typing every invite.

Method: primary vendor docs opened with WebFetch or curl on 2026-10-02. Each row records the URL and the page date when the page shows one, else "accessed 2026-10-02". Status legend:
- FETCHED: the claim was read on the page cited.
- SEARCH ONLY: the claim came from a WebSearch summary and the page could not be opened. Marked [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- NOT RUN: the check was not done, with the reason.

Note on tooling: the session WebSearch budget (200 calls) ran out during this topic. The remaining items were checked with WebFetch or curl on known URLs only. Nothing below relies on a URL that was not opened, except rows marked SEARCH ONLY.

---

### 2.1 Delegated IT setup link: WorkOS Admin Portal

What it is: a hosted setup UI that the vendor's customer hands to its own IT contact, so IT configures SSO, directory sync (SCIM), domain verification and related items without a call with the vendor.

Mechanics (all FETCHED, accessed 2026-10-02):
- Two kinds of link. Dashboard link: "Can be revoked; Automatically revoked on setup completion; Expires after 30 days"; the dashboard "Invite IT contact" button can email the setup link automatically. API link: "Portal links expire 5 minutes after they're created, so we recommend redirecting users immediately (i.e. don't email the user Portal links)." Source: https://workos.com/docs/admin-portal
- API: `POST /portal/generate_link` with an organization and an `intent`. Allowed intents: `sso`, `dsync`, `audit_logs`, `log_streams`, `domain_verification`, `certificate_renewal`, `bring_your_own_key`. Optional `return_url`, `success_url`, and `it_contact_emails` ("Accepts up to 20 emails"). Source: https://workos.com/docs/reference/admin-portal/portal-link
- IT sees "custom walk-through documentation for each identity provider" with an IdP picker, so they can "onboard their organizations without high-touch support". Source: https://workos.com/docs/admin-portal
- Domain verification inside the portal: IT adds a DNS TXT record; WorkOS "automatically identifies the DNS provider and tailors guidance", marks the domain verified and dispatches an event to the app. Source: https://workos.com/docs/domain-verification
- Group-to-role mapping by the customer: "Groups usually correspond to roles in your app. Therefore, IT contacts will often map a group one-to-one to a role." When enabled in the Admin Portal, IT contacts configure these mappings themselves; new users added to a mapped group get that role automatically. Source: https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/identity-provider-role-assignment
- JIT: "JIT provisioning automatically creates users and organization memberships when a user signs in", for users whose email domain matches a verified organization domain or domain policy. Source: https://workos.com/docs/user-management/jit-provisioning
- Outcome evidence: no numbers published. Customer quote only (Prefect): "Our UI gives customers a link; they go to the Admin Portal, complete onboarding steps at their leisure, and never have to talk to us". Source: https://workos.com/admin-portal (accessed 2026-10-02). The WorkOS blog of 2022-02-28 (Mahmoud Abdelwahab) states the problem ("painful coordination between developers and their enterprise customers") but gives no Admin Portal metric: https://workos.com/blog/frictionless-enterprise-customer-onboarding-using-the-workos-admin-portal

Metis transfer: the Metis tenant admin should not do SSO, SCIM, domain verification or IdP group-to-role mapping alone. Give them "Send to IT" links scoped to one intent each (sso, scim, domains, role mapping), with IT contact emails, auto-revoke on completion and a 30-day expiry, and let the workspace build continue in parallel on password plus MFA.

### 2.2 IdP catalogs: Okta Integration Network (OIN) and Microsoft Entra app gallery

What a listing gives the customer admin: the app appears in the IdP's own catalog with SSO (and optionally provisioning) settings preconfigured, so the admin adds it and fills only tenant-specific values.

Okta (all FETCHED, accessed 2026-10-02):
- "OIN integrations speed adoption by simplifying admin configuration steps and reducing friction." Accepted types include OIDC, SAML 2.0, SCIM, Workflows connectors and others. Submission runs through the OIN Wizard, then Okta review. Source: https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/submit-app-overview/
- Requirements: "Your app integration must support multi-tenancy to be listed in the public OIN catalog"; "SAML integrations must use SHA256"; OIDC uses the org authorization server only; "The OIN Wizard is only available in Integrator Free Plan orgs"; a customer configuration guide must be reachable by URL. Source: https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/submit-app-prereq/main/
- Customer admin flow: Applications > Browse App Catalog > search > Add integration; OIN integrations "only require the administrator to add the integration and configure it to work with their particular Okta instance." Source: https://help.okta.com/en-us/content/topics/apps/apps-add-applications.htm
- Catalog size: the integrations page showed 8,377 integrations, 7,826 tagged SSO and 947 tagged Lifecycle Management (live count read 2026-10-02). Source: https://www.okta.com/integrations/

Microsoft Entra (all FETCHED):
- Gallery = "thousands of applications that are preintegrated" for SSO and automated provisioning. Listed benefits include "Configuration of the application is simple and minimal" and step-by-step tutorials. For SAML gallery apps, Create adds the app to the tenant; for OIDC gallery apps, the admin signs in to the vendor app to add it (consent). One instance per tenant. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/overview-application-gallery (ms.date 2026-01-05)
- SSO requirements: OIDC must be multitenant (or one instance per customer); recommended: read IdP metadata from the Entra URL because this "reduces customer configuration and supports certificate rotation"; provide UI and APIs for customers to configure SSO; provide a way to enforce SSO tenant-wide with a bypass for admins and emergency access. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/app-gallery-sso-requirements (ms.date 2026-08-26)
- SCIM requirements: SCIM 2.0 users (required) and groups (recommended); "at least 25 requests per second per tenant"; OAuth 2.0 client credentials or workload identity federation (no basic auth, no long-lived bearer tokens); ISV requirement: "Deploy your SCIM provisioning integration to at least 100 mutual customers by using the Microsoft Entra non-gallery approach." Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/app-gallery-user-provisioning-requirements (ms.date 2026-08-26)
- Publishing is now self-service with Microsoft review. Example timeline on the page: review "within 5 business days", Preview "within 10 business days", public "within 7 business days". Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/publish-app-gallery (ms.date 2026-08-24)
- Shared prerequisites: Partner One ID, test tenant, and public customer docs that state "Roles required to configure the integration". Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/v2-howto-app-gallery-listing (ms.date 2026-09-02)

Metis transfer: an OIN and Entra gallery listing turns customer SSO from "exchange metadata with the vendor" into "add Metis from the catalog". It is a roadmap item, not a launch item: Entra requires 100 mutual SCIM customers before a gallery SCIM listing. Until then, the delegated setup link (2.1) with a metadata-URL import does the same job.

### 2.3 Verified domains, domain capture, approved domains and JIT

Common shape: (1) an admin proves domain ownership with DNS (sometimes an HTTPS file); (2) a policy decides what happens to people with that email domain: join automatically, request to join, or be forced to SSO; (3) optionally, a default role or seat is applied.

| Product | Admin action | What happens to people on the domain | Source (date) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slack (Free, Pro, Business+) | Admin > Workspace settings > "Let people with approved email addresses join this workspace" | They join via the sign-up link or by entering their email; member invitation requests for approved addresses are "approved automatically"; "Enabling single sign-on (SSO) will override your workspace signup preferences." | https://slack.com/help/articles/115004856503-Manage-how-people-join-your-workspace (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Slack Enterprise | Org Owner claims domains | People trying to create a separate workspace on the domain get "a message (with a contact link included) directing them to contact an Org Admin"; new people can create an account through SSO; the domain is removed from sign-up of outside workspaces; contact link defaults to the Org Primary Owner. | https://slack.com/help/articles/115001379947-Claim-domains-for-an-Enterprise-organization (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Figma (Organization, Enterprise) | Org admin adds DNS TXT, turns on domain capture | "People who sign up for Figma from verified domains are automatically added as members"; existing users on the domain are added and their drafts move; subdomains need separate verification. Verified domain: "Members are not required to complete email verification during sign-in." | https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360045953273-Manage-domain-capture-for-an-organization ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040532333-Guide-to-SAML-SSO (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Notion (all plans for allowed domains) | Settings > General > Trusted domain access > Allowed email domains | People on the domain "automatically join your workspace as members, or as workspace owners if you're on a Free Plan"; only domains already used by existing members can be added. | https://www.notion.com/help/workspace-settings (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Notion (Enterprise verified domains) | Org settings > add domain > DNS TXT | One domain per organization; subdomains separate; DNS can take up to 72 hours; verification codes expire after one week; owners control who may create workspaces and can claim workspaces created on the domain. | https://www.notion.com/help/domain-management (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Notion (SAML JIT) | Turn on automatic account creation in SAML setup | People signing in via SAML join as members automatically; Notion: "We don't recommend enabling Just-in Time provisioning if you are using SCIM". Business: 1 SAML configuration; Enterprise: up to 25. | https://www.notion.com/help/saml-sso-configuration (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Atlassian (verify and claim) | Directory > Domains: DNS TXT (up to 72 hours) or HTTPS file | Claim all accounts automatically or upload a CSV ("up to 10,000 email addresses in each CSV file", max 5MB); users are told the organization manages their account. | https://support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/verify-a-domain-to-manage-accounts/ (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Atlassian (approved domains) | Apps > App access settings > add domain, choose roles per app | With "Required" unticked, users from the domain "can join your app instantly"; ticked, they request access and an admin approves. Invitation links "automatically expire after 30 days". | https://support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/control-how-users-get-access-to-products/ (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Zoom (Business, Enterprise, Education) | Account Profile > Associated Domains; verify by TXT, HTML file, meta tag or manual approval via support (about one hour to several days) | "Manage users with the same domain" restricts new account creation; consolidation prompts existing users to join or change email, "allowing up to three sign-ins before forced action"; option to require SSO for the domain. | https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0066259 (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Linear | Settings: approved email domains; invite with role | Matching addresses "join the workspace without an invitation or approval"; inviter picks Member, Guest or Admin on paid plans; invite links are persistent and reusable, with a reset button. | https://linear.app/docs/invite-members (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| WorkOS (for vendors) | Domain policy plus verified domain | JIT creates the user and the organization membership at first sign-in. | https://workos.com/docs/user-management/jit-provisioning (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Miro (Enterprise) | Domain control after DNS verification | New sign-ups on the domain can request access, join automatically, or join and be blocked from creating teams; JIT requires SSO; existing users are not moved. | https://help.miro.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034831793-Domain-control | SEARCH ONLY, page returned HTTP 403. [Unverified - confirm before applying] |

Timing evidence that matters for a 30-minute target: DNS verification can take "up to 72 hours" (Atlassian, Notion), and Zoom quotes about one hour to several days by method. Sources above, FETCHED. Implication: domain verification cannot sit on the critical path of a 30-minute setup.

Metis transfer: let the first admin type the company domain once; verify it in the background (delegate the DNS step to IT via 2.1); meanwhile offer an "approved domain" policy with a default workspace role (for example Viewer) and an approval toggle, so colleagues self-join instead of being invited one by one.

### 2.4 Invite-your-team loops and what the evidence says

Mechanics (FETCHED):
- Slack invite links are "active for 30 days" and "can be used by up to 400 people"; by default members (not guests) can invite; admins can switch to "invitations require admin approval", where members request invitations. https://slack.com/help/articles/201330256-Invite-new-members-to-your-workspace (accessed 2026-10-02)
- Figma: "Any member or guest can invite someone to a resource at or below their permission level"; people invited at org level get a View seat; SAML adds a provisional account when the user is added in the IdP. https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040453113-Add-members-or-guests-to-an-organization (accessed 2026-10-02)
- Atlassian user invite settings range from "Invite anyone" to "Don't allow invites", with "Require admin approval" in between. https://support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/control-how-users-get-access-to-products/ (accessed 2026-10-02)
- Slack sign-up flow (secondary teardown): if the user tries to skip the invite step, "Slack pops up a modal that gently talks you out of it, and even tips you that most people start by inviting just one or two team members"; task cards in default channels prompt inviting teammates. Userpilot, Lisa Ballantyne, published 2026-06-29, updated 2026-08-13: https://userpilot.com/blog/slack-onboarding/ (FETCHED; secondary observation, not Slack data)

Evidence on whether invites drive retention:
- Slack, founder statement: "Based on experience of which companies stuck with us and which didn't, we decided that any team that has exchanged 2,000 messages in its history has tried Slack"; "after 2,000 messages, 93% of those customers are still using Slack today." Method: founder judgement from observed cohorts, no analysis published. First Round Review, 2015-02-27: https://review.firstround.com/from-0-to-1b-slacks-founder-shares-their-epic-launch-strategy/ (FETCHED)
- CustomerScore: "Single-user accounts churn 14 to 33x faster than teams" (page text uses a dash range, rewritten here); about 44,000 users across participating companies; multipliers compare segments within the same product; company data not disclosed. Patrik Chalupa, 2026-06-25: https://www.customerscore.io/blog/saas-retention-statistics-44000-users (FETCHED). Quality: vendor analysis, observational, measures seats per account, not invites sent.
- PostHog (counter-evidence): "we want users to invite teammates, but we found that doing so doesn't mean they stick around, so optimizing this isn't the best use of our time." Their activation metric for session replay: watching 5 or more replays and setting a replay filter at least once, defined against being active 3 months after start. Raquel M Smith, 2024-11-28: https://posthog.com/product-engineers/activation-metrics (FETCHED via curl). Quality: practitioner internal analysis, no numbers published.
- GitLab public experiment design: invites as an optional step in account setup; metrics: invites sent, week-4 retention and week-4 upgrade versus control; expected "increase the rate at which free accounts invite colleagues by 5%". No result recorded on the issue. https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/growth/product/-/work_items/150 (FETCHED, no date shown)

Reading: multi-user accounts retain better (correlational), but an invite count alone is not a proven lever. What counts is invitees doing work.

Metis transfer: do not measure "invites sent". Invite people into a specific job (approve this gate, confirm this budget, own this project) so the invitee's first session ends in an action. Bound invite rights by role ("at or below their permission level", as in Figma).

### 2.5 Distributing setup tasks to many stakeholders

| Product | What is distributed | Mechanics | Source (date) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lattice (review cycles) | Choosing peer reviewers | Employees nominate peers; managers get a "Select peer reviewers" task, then Nominate and "Submit and approve"; admin overrides lock manager edits. If the manager has not approved by the end of peer selection, "the nominations submitted will lock in and automatically be approved." | https://help.lattice.com/hc/en-us/articles/360062344173-Nominate-Peer-Reviewers-for-Your-Direct-Reports ; https://help.lattice.com/en-us/articles/15179229-what-happens-if-a-manager-hasn-t-approved-nominations-before-peer-selection-ends (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED (curl) |
| Culture Amp (unified performance cycle) | Peer nominations, upward feedback assignment | Optional nomination limit (for example 5), bulk approval when a limit is set; "Upward Feedback Automation" removes manual assignment; each step has a "Soft Communicated Closure"; optional "Approve Nominations" date "When peer nominations are automatically approved, provided the manager hasn't already requested feedback". | https://support.cultureamp.com/en/articles/10398426-launch-a-unified-performance-review-cycle (accessed 2026-10-02, page says updated this week) | FETCHED (curl) |
| HubSpot | The vendor's own setup checklist | "Use checklists to manage HubSpot onboarding and setup by working through predefined tasks"; checklists and single tasks have an Assignee (only users with Marketing access); "All Tasks" view filters by checklist, assignee, status, due date. | https://knowledge.hubspot.com/help-and-resources/manage-onboarding-to-do-lists-with-checklists (last updated 2026-05-29) | FETCHED |
| Gusto (embedded payroll) | Employee personal, tax and bank data | Admin onboarding versus self-onboarding: in self-onboarding the employee enters their own data, then the employer reviews and answers "employer-relevant state tax questions" that only the employer can answer; statuses include `self_onboarding_invited`, `self_onboarding_invited_overdue`, `self_onboarding_completed_by_employee`. | https://docs.gusto.com/embedded-payroll/docs/onboarding-method-comparison (updated 2026-06-09) | FETCHED |
| BambooHR | New-hire tasks for IT, managers, new hire | Admin can change due dates and assignees per task; "By default, assignees will be notified 15 minutes after the Onboarding task is assigned, on the due date, or on a day before the due date." | https://www.bamboohr.com/product-updates/onboarding-task-and-notifications-updates (no date shown, accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Rippling (dogfooding blog) | HR, IT and payroll steps per hire | Four recruits onboarded: "Within ten minutes, every app was unlocked, permissions were enabled, training was assigned and laptops were on their way"; "I only get pinged when something genuinely needs my attention". Vendor anecdote, n = 4, no method. | https://www.rippling.com/blog/inside-rippling-10-minute-onboarding (Sinead Reilly, 2026-03-26) | FETCHED (curl) |
| Workday onboarding tasks | n/a | NOT RUN: WebSearch budget exhausted; the guessed public product URL returned 404; Workday docs need a customer login. | n/a | NOT RUN |

Patterns that repeat: (a) each task goes to the person who owns the answer; (b) a pre-filled default or proposal exists, so the owner confirms instead of authoring; (c) soft deadlines plus an automatic approval date, so silence does not block the cycle (Lattice, Culture Amp); (d) the coordinator sees progress by assignee (HubSpot); (e) the coordinator keeps the few decisions only they can make (Gusto employer tax questions).

Metis transfer: split workspace setup into owner tasks with pre-filled proposals: finance owner confirms currency, fiscal calendar and budget categories; each gate approver confirms membership and quorum for their gate; PMO lead confirms the lifecycle; project managers complete charter fields. Each task has a soft deadline and an auto-accept date; the setup owner sees a by-assignee tracker and handles exceptions only.

### 2.6 Ask-the-owner patterns

| Product | Trigger | Who is asked, and how | Source (date) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft Entra admin consent workflow | User cannot consent to an app | "they can send a request for admin approval. The request is sent via email to admins who are designated as reviewers"; reviewers need the right permissions (designation does not elevate); configurable "Consent request expires after (days)" with a reminder roughly mid-way; enabling "can take up to an hour". | https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-admin-consent-workflow (ms.date 2024-12-29, updated 2026-02-19) | FETCHED |
| Slack app approval | Member wants an app that is not pre-approved | Member requests the app (owners can require a comment); requests go to Workspace Owners via Slack notifications; owners can appoint app managers; available on all plans. | https://slack.com/help/articles/222386767-Manage-app-approval-for-your-workspace (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Slack invitation requests | Member wants to add someone | With admin approval on, members request invitations for admins to approve or deny; for approved domains the request is approved automatically. | https://slack.com/help/articles/201330256-Invite-new-members-to-your-workspace ; https://slack.com/help/articles/115004856503-Manage-how-people-join-your-workspace (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Slack claimed domain | Someone tries to start a separate workspace | Shown a contact link to an Org Admin (default: Org Primary Owner email). | https://slack.com/help/articles/115001379947-Claim-domains-for-an-Enterprise-organization (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Figma seat requests | User needs a higher seat | Admins get "both an email and in-app notification"; the request shows where it was sent from, reason, current seat, time and cost; approval policy: "Manually approve seats", "Manually approve, unless seat is available" (default) or "Auto-approve seats". | https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/1500003870721-Approve-or-decline-seat-upgrade-requests ; https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/4414038570007-Set-approval-settings-for-new-seats (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Notion request access | User lacks access to a page | "This will notify the page's creators or editors, who can choose to accept or deny your access request"; edit-access requests go to the page creator. | https://www.notion.com/help/sharing-and-permissions (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |
| Atlassian access requests | User from a domain that requires approval | User requests access; org admins approve or deny; admins choose when they are notified. | https://support.atlassian.com/user-management/docs/control-how-users-get-access-to-products/ (accessed 2026-10-02) | FETCHED |

Metis transfer: when a user hits something they cannot set (an option list, a gate rule, the AI access policy), show "Ask the owner" with the request context pre-filled (what, why, cost or impact), route it to the named owner, and let the admin pick an approval policy once (manual, auto unless risky, auto), as Figma does for seats.

- Rippling and BambooHR official help-center articles: not opened; claims above use the vendor blog and product-update pages only.
- No source found that measures how much a delegated IT link (WorkOS or similar) shortens SSO setup; WorkOS publishes quotes, not numbers.
- No source found that directly measures the effect of "approved domain" self-join on team activation.

### 2.10 Top transferable ideas for Metis

1. Take tenant access off the critical path with delegated, scoped setup links. The Metis admin sends IT one link per job (SSO, SCIM, domain verification, IdP group-to-role mapping), with IT contact emails, auto-revoke on completion and a 30-day expiry. The workspace build continues on password plus MFA, because DNS verification alone can take up to 72 hours. Add OIN and Entra gallery listings later (Entra SCIM needs 100 mutual customers first).
2. Replace invite lists and solo authoring with self-join plus owner micro-tasks that auto-accept. An approved domain with a default role lets colleagues join on their own (Slack, Atlassian, Linear). Configuration is sent as small pre-filled proposals to the people who own the answers (gate approvers, finance, PMO, PMs), each with a soft deadline and an auto-accept date (Lattice, Culture Amp). The setup owner tracks progress by assignee (HubSpot) and handles exceptions only (Rippling).

### 3.1 AI-assisted spreadsheet import and column mapping (embeddable importers)

#### Flatfile

What it does: embeddable and headless data import with AI column mapping, value (enum) mapping, validation and transformation.

Mechanics:
- Mapping suggestions come from "machine-learning models trained on millions of historical mappings", generated "based on the column names and values in the source data"; covers field mapping and enum mapping; "The Flatfile platform remembers your previously chosen mappings and will suggest them when it sees similar schemas / data in the future". Source: https://flatfile.com/docs/legacy-docs/concepts/mapping (accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.
- Current product page: engine "trained on 5B+ mapping decisions" and can "learn from past imports". Source: https://flatfile.com/product/mapping/ (accessed 2026-10-02), fetched. No accuracy figure or method on the page.
- Automap plugin for headless imports: accuracy option 'confident' means "All mapped fields must have a confidence level of 'strong' (> 90%) or 'absolute' (100%)"; 'exact' means "All mapped fields must have a confidence level of 'absolute' (100%)". An `onFailure` callback runs "if the automapping process is aborted due to low mapping confidence". It is "intended for use in a server-side listener, not in the browser." Source: https://flatfile.com/docs/plugins/automap (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.
- Mapping screen grouping (Recommendations, Exact Matches, Previously Mapped, Unmapped, Empty Fields). Source: https://flatfile.com/blog/advanced-mapping-a-new-essential-tool-for-data-migration-teams/ : search summary only, page body did not load [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Numbers: homepage "Use Flatfile to move customer data into your systems 70% faster". Source: https://flatfile.com/ (accessed 2026-10-02), fetched. Vendor claim, method not stated. "5B+ mapping decisions" and "millions of historical mappings" describe training-data scale, not accuracy.

Metis transfer: auto-commit a mapping only above a confidence gate and fall back to a human review step when any field is below it; this lets a repeat import (monthly capacity or budget file) run without a person while a first import stays reviewed.

#### OneSchema

What it does: embeddable CSV and spreadsheet importer with templates, validators, AI mapping and AI-generated validation and transformation code.

Mechanics (source https://docs.oneschema.co/docs/ai-bundle, updated 2026-05-23, fetched):
- Auto-mapping strategy is a configurable combination of "exact", "fuzzy" and "historical".
- AI "Suggested Column Mappings" map the template columns left unmapped; users approve before continuing.
- AI picklist mapping converts uploaded values to picklist values (example: "United States" to "US").
- AI generates validation code from natural language and generates transformation code.
- Review flag: "A star will appear next to mappings created using AI so users can easily verify mappings."
- Privacy: "Your data is never used to train the underlying models"; sample CSV rows and file context are shared for processing; external LLM providers retain data for 30 days for abuse monitoring; partners named: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google.
- Product page: "Set your mappings once and bypass mapping on future uploads. In fact, we use historical mappings across your entire use base to intelligently suggest the best mappings to your user." Source: https://www.oneschema.co/embeddable-importer (accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.
- Numbers on the same page: "90%" labelled "IMPORT CONVERSION RATE", "6 mo." labelled "ENGINEERING TIME SAVED", "100%" labelled "REDUCE SUPPORT TICKETS", "Validate and transform files of up to 4GB in under 1 second", "Performant for files up to 20M rows". Vendor claims, method not stated.
- Validation webhooks (customer API used as a column validator that can return suggested values) and headless mapping via `POST /v1/embeds/{embed_id}/map`: https://docs.oneschema.co/docs/validation-webhook and https://docs.oneschema.co/docs/initialize-importer-through-api, search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying].

Metis transfer: mark every AI-made mapping visibly (the star) so a PMO lead can audit the 10 percent the machine guessed instead of re-checking everything; reuse a tenant's historical mappings so the second budget or risk register upload maps itself.

#### Dromo

What it does: embeddable importer (React, Angular, Vue, JS) with fuzzy and AI column matching, hooks for validation, AI transformations, and a headless mode.

Mechanics:
- Settings (https://developer.dromo.io/settings, accessed 2026-10-02, fetched): `autoMapHeaders`: "Dromo will try to automatically map the CSV headers to fields based off of previous uploads with the same importIdentifier"; `matchingStep.fuzzyMatchHeaders`; `matchingStep.matchToSchema` (user matches only schema fields, useful when the file has many irrelevant columns); `invalidDataBehavior` with `BLOCK_SUBMIT` ("Dromo will disable the 'Finish' button preventing the user from submitting with errors"), `REMOVE_INVALID_ROWS` ("Dromo will remove any rows with errors and the user will see a dialog") and `INCLUDE_INVALID_ROWS`; `reviewStep.enableNavigatingErrors` (step through errors one at a time with inline fixes); `reviewStep.highlightAutoFixes` (highlights cells changed by automatic transformations); `savePartialSession`: "Dromo will automatically save user progress throughout the import flow, allowing users to resume their session".
- AI matching (https://developer.dromo.io/faqs, fetched): "We harness OpenAI to assist users in the mapping process"; column header information is sent to Dromo servers for this; Private Mode keeps file processing in the browser.
- Hooks (https://developer.dromo.io/reference/hooks, fetched): "Column hooks run first and only once after the 'column matching' stage", suited to "API lookups or data enrichment for entire columns"; row hooks run in "init" mode before review and again in "update" mode after the user edits; recommended pattern: "make any API calls in a column hook and then validate that the data remains correct using a row hook in `update` mode."
- AI Transform Data (https://developer.dromo.io/guides/using-transform-data, fetched): users "create bulk transformations from natural language"; Pro plan; "the result is previewed to the user so they can optionally accept or reject it"; "The AI building the transformation function never has access to the import data"; a transformation only sees one row at a time.
- Numbers on https://dromo.io/ (accessed 2026-10-02, fetched): "Reduce onboarding errors by 98%", "Save more than a year of engineering time", "Migrate in less than an hour", "Integration typically takes less than 30 minutes". Vendor claims, method not stated. Also "Dromo uses GPT to automatically map imported columns to your schema".

Metis transfer: a "resume later" import session and a guided "next error" navigator suit the reality that a PMO admin often needs a finance or resource owner to fix a few rows; the hook pattern (lookup once, revalidate on edit) fits checking imported project managers or cost centres against the tenant directory.

#### nuvo, now Ingestro

What it does: embeddable importer SDK with AI column matching, option (value) mapping and an end-to-end "Contextual Engine".

Mechanics:
- Rename: https://docs.getnuvo.com/sdk/release-notes/ returns HTTP 301 to https://docs.ingestro.com/sdk/release-notes/ (observed 2026-10-02); the v4.0.1 notes say "Renamed component from `<NuvoImporter>` to `<DataImporter>` / `nuvo-importer` to `data-importer`." Fetched.
- Overview (https://docs.ingestro.com/sdk/overview/, accessed 2026-10-02, fetched): "Our Ingestro AI restructures the data and matches the imported columns to the columns in your defined output schema." "It learns from initial imports, so if a similar file structure is uploaded in the future, this step can be skipped." "users can confirm recommended matches and create new mappings if necessary." Three steps: upload, match columns, review entries (errors fixed manually or with AI data cleaning).
- v3.0.1 release notes, dated 22.04.2025 (https://docs.ingestro.com/sdk/release-notes-v3/, fetched): `columnMappingConfiguration` "Allows defining where column mapping should run (`"browser"` or `"node"`), which matching layers to apply (`"exact"`, `"historic"`, `"smart"`, `"fuzzy"`), and the confidence threshold for accepting matches"; `optionMappingConfiguration` gives the same control for option mapping of category columns; `contextualEngine` enables "automatic end-to-end import handling, including mapping, transforming, and cleaning data", with modes `"enabled"` (runs after upload) and `"prompt"` (user chooses engine or manual flow).
- `alternativeMatches` (synonyms and abbreviations used in similarity scoring): search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- No accuracy or time-saved figures found on the pages opened.

Metis transfer: let the customer choose "do it for me" (auto engine) or "let me map" at the start of an import; experts and novices both finish faster.

#### Osmos (acquired by Microsoft)

- Microsoft announced the acquisition on 2026-01-05: Osmos is "an agentic AI data engineering platform designed to help simplify complex and time-consuming data workflows" and "The Osmos team will join Microsoft's Fabric engineering organization". Source: https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/01/05/microsoft-announces-acquisition-of-osmos-to-accelerate-autonomous-data-engineering-in-fabric/ (2026-01-05), fetched.
- Osmos products "will be sunset starting in January 2026" (Osmos FAQ quoted by press; GeekWire reports Uploaders, Pipelines and Datasets included). Sources: https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsoft-acquires-data-analytics-seattle-startup-osmos-to-fuel-push-into-autonomous-data-engineering/ (HTTP 403), https://www.sdxcentral.com/news/microsoft-ingests-osmos-to-boost-fabric-agentic-ai-abilities/ : search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Uploader features formerly documented (AutoMap "uses generative AI to significantly reduce the need for manual column mapping", example "MSRP" to "Price"; `autoMapEnabled`; `autoRecallEnabled` to reuse transforms from earlier uploads; `allowSubmissionWithErrors`; AI Value Mapping to enums; Standard mode for external users, Advanced mode for internal teams): https://docs.osmos.io/data-transformations/column-mapping-and-data-cleanup-panel and https://docs.osmos.io/developer-docs/optional-uploader-settings now redirect (HTTP 307) to a GitBook app page with no content; www.osmos.io failed with a certificate mismatch. Search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying].

Metis transfer: do not depend on Osmos as a vendor; the Standard (external user) versus Advanced (internal implementer) split is still a useful pattern for Metis: a simple mapper for customer admins and a richer one for Metis or partner implementers.

#### Cross-vendor synthesis (AI mapping)

All five converge on the same pipeline, which Metis can copy without buying any of them:
1. Layered matching: exact name, fuzzy or synonym, historical memory (per customer or across the user base), then AI suggestion (Flatfile, OneSchema, Dromo, Ingestro).
2. Confidence gate: auto-accept above a threshold, otherwise human review (Flatfile Automap >90 percent "strong"; Ingestro configurable threshold).
3. Value mapping, not only column mapping: picklists, enums, statuses (OneSchema, Flatfile, Ingestro option mapping).
4. AI work is labelled and reviewable (OneSchema star, Dromo `highlightAutoFixes`, Dromo transform preview with accept or reject).
5. Privacy posture stated: headers or sample rows only, no model training on customer data (OneSchema, Dromo Private Mode, Dromo transform AI never sees data).
6. Memory: the second import of the same shaped file needs no mapping (Dromo `importIdentifier`, OneSchema historical, Ingestro "this step can be skipped", ClickUp workspace memory in 3.3).

No vendor published a mapping accuracy figure with a method. Every outcome number found (Flatfile 70 percent faster, Dromo 98 percent fewer errors, OneSchema 90 percent import conversion) is a vendor claim with no method stated.

Parsing library: MPXJ reads "MPX, MPP, MSPDI, MPD, Planner, Primavera P6 PMXML and XER, Primavera P3, SureTrak, Asta Powerproject" and more, can read from "Microsoft Project Server, Microsoft Planner, Primavera P6 Web Services (P6 EPPM), and Oracle Primavera Cloud (OPC)", is "written and maintained in Java" with .NET, Ruby and Python wrappers, and is "distributed under the terms of the GNU LGPL". Source: https://www.mpxj.org/ (accessed 2026-10-02), fetched. Licence fit for a SaaS backend needs legal review [Unverified - confirm before applying].

Format reference: Microsoft's Project XML Data Interchange schema ("mspdi_pj12.xsd") is the documented XML format Project uses "for exchanging data with other applications". Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office-project/xml-data-interchange/introduction-to-project-xml-data (ms.date 2018-03-14), fetched.

Synthesis:
- Every tool loses something. The common casualties are calendars and exceptions, non-default baselines, the resource pool, custom fields and time-phased data (Celoxis list; Wrike custom fields; Microsoft unsupported features; Smartsheet constraints).
- The better imports say exactly what was dropped or changed (Microsoft "Import complete" message), leave the source untouched and allow delete and retry (Microsoft), and resolve people at import time by mapping MS Project resource names to user accounts (Wrike, Celoxis, ProjectManager).
- XML (MSPDI) is the safer path than binary .mpp in several tools (Smartsheet workaround, AdaptiveWork XML only).

Metis transfer: an .mpp or MSPDI import that creates the project, WBS, dependencies, milestones and assignments in one step, maps resource names to people (or placeholders) and ends with a fidelity report ("kept, changed, dropped") before commit, removes the single largest manual setup job (rebuilding WBS with assignments) for Project Online refugees.

### 3.3 Imports from Smartsheet, Jira, Excel and other work tools

#### Jira Cloud CSV importer
Source: https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/create-issues-using-the-csv-importer/ (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.
- Steps: choose CSV and an existing configuration if available; map CSV column headers to Jira fields (Summary is mandatory); map specific CSV values to Jira field values; Begin import.
- Dry run: "Select Validate before importing" to "check for errors or warnings".
- Reuse: "You can save your configuration for future imports with similar settings."
- Diagnostics: "you can download a detailed log."
- Value mapping tip: "leave a field cleared or clear any content within it to import the value as is."
- Limits: non-administrators can import 250 work items per CSV file; the bulk-create option cannot map parent-child hierarchies (use the external system import instead).

Metis transfer: a "Validate" button that runs the full import logic without writing, plus a downloadable mapping profile the customer can reuse, are cheap to build and remove fear of a bad import.

#### Jira import directly from monday.com
Source: https://support.atlassian.com/jira-work-management/docs/import-data-directly-from-monday-into-jira-work-management (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.

Metis transfer: let the importer ask one structural question ("what do your groups mean: phases, programs or statuses?") so a flat board becomes a Metis program, project and WBS tree.

Source: https://help.meisterplan.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004430413-Import-Your-Data-into-Meisterplan (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.
- Round trip: export to Excel (select date range, scenario and portfolio), edit, paste back through Quick Import; caveats: date formats can fail when Office and browser locales differ; milestone dependencies, Project Key and rank cannot be updated this way. Source: https://help.meisterplan.com/hc/en-us/articles/4529961358108-Updating-Projects-Using-Microsoft-Excel (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.

Metis transfer: copy and paste from any spreadsheet into a validating grid is the lowest-friction path for capacity, allocations, budgets and risks; importing into a scenario rather than the plan of record makes the first import safe to try.

#### Smartsheet Resource Management bulk project import (upsert by key)
- "Resource Management provides spreadsheet templates so you can add or update multiple projects at once." New projects: leave Project ID blank; "To update attributes for existing projects leave the Project ID intact"; new and updated projects can be combined in one file; save as "CSV UTF-8"; "Each project must have a Project Name and Project Type. All other fields are optional."; "If there were errors during the import, the email includes a link to the status page." Source: https://help.smartsheet.com/articles/2481126-import-multiple-projects (no page date, accessed 2026-10-02), fetched.

Metis transfer: a downloadable template per object (project, budget line, allocation, risk) with a stable ID column that switches between create and update lets the same file seed the portfolio and later refresh it.
