### 3.6 Top transferable ideas for Metis (data import)

1. "Bring your plan" importer with a fidelity report. Accept .mpp and MSPDI XML (an MPXJ-class parser), Excel or CSV, and exports from Smartsheet, Jira, monday and Asana. Map in layers (exact, synonyms, tenant memory, AI suggestion) with a confidence gate and visible AI marks; ask one structural question (what do groups or outline levels mean) to build the portfolio, program, project and WBS tree; map resource names to people or to placeholders that bind on invite; end with a "kept, changed, dropped" report before commit. Bottlenecks: existing data, people and access. Timely because Project Online retired on 2026-09-30.
2. Validate, commit to a draft, undo. Every import (projects, budgets, capacity, allocations, risks) runs a no-write validation grid with row-blocking versus field-level errors, upserts by a stable key from downloadable templates, lands in a scenario or draft rather than the plan of record, tags records with an import batch id and offers "undo this import" for a fixed window. Bottleneck: existing data; also lowers the fear that slows first imports.


## 4. Configuration packs and configuration as code

Scope: how enterprise SaaS vendors let a customer start from a prebuilt configuration (packages, templates, blueprints, implementation packs) and how they let admins preview, apply, version and roll back configuration (update sets, plan and apply, YAML or JSON import and export).

Method and conventions
- Access date for every web source below: 2026-10-02, unless a publication or last-modified date is given.
- Verification status per claim: "fetched" means the primary page was opened with WebFetch (or the PDF was read) and the quote or fact was taken from it. "search summary only" means the claim was seen only in a WebSearch summary, the page was not opened (or it returned HTTP 403 or 404), and the claim carries [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Numbers from vendor marketing that state no method are labelled "vendor claim, method not stated".
- NOT RUN items: WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted (200 of 200) part way through this topic, so some sub-items could not be searched. They are listed in 4.9 with the reason.

### 4.1 Salesforce: packages, industry clouds, guided setup

**Unlocked and second-generation managed packages (2GP)**
- What it does: a package is a versioned container of metadata (objects, fields, Apex, flows, pages, layouts, permission sets) that is installed into an org.
- Mechanics, fetched from Trailhead "Unlocked Packages for Customers" unit (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/unlocked-packages-for-customers/break-up-your-metadata, accessed 2026-10-02):
  - "Each version is an immutable artifact, a snapshot of the contents of your package." Version number example "1.3.0.2".
  - Source of truth: "the new and improved source of truth is your version control system."
  - "You can install a package version in any org: a scratch org, sandbox org, or production org."
  - Upgrade semantics: "The installation of any new package version overwrites the changes made directly in the production org."
  - Promotion path: after QA, "install this version in your sandbox for user acceptance testing (UAT), and eventually in production."
- 2GP, fetched from Trailhead 2GP unit (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/second-generation-managed-packages/learn-about-secondgeneration-managed-packaging, accessed 2026-10-02): "A package is a container for an app that you plan to sell and distribute to Salesforce customers"; can include "Apex classes, custom fields, custom objects, Flows, Lightning pages, and page layouts"; each version "is an immutable artifact"; namespace prefixes component API names (example FinanceX__EnhancedAccount__c); customers "can upgrade to newer versions independently or receive pushed upgrades."
- Note: developer.salesforce.com documentation pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch and to curl, so packaging guide pages were not opened directly.
- Metis transfer: package a lifecycle framework (stages, gates, approvers, quorum rules, mandatory artifacts, conditional rules) as an immutable, numbered version; projects pin to a version, and upgrades are explicit.

**Install into a sandbox first (AppExchange)**
- Fetched: Trailhead "Install AgentExchange Packages" (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/appexchange_basics/appexchange_basics_install, accessed 2026-10-02). Salesforce now brands AppExchange as "AgentExchange" on Trailhead.
  - "AgentExchange experts never install in production without testing in a Developer Edition org or a sandbox first."
  - Install access choice: "admins only, all users, or specific profiles."
  - Managed packages: "The provider can automatically upgrade the solution." Unmanaged: "you must uninstall the package from your org and then reinstall a new version."
- Metis transfer: install any pack into a draft (unpublished) copy of the workspace first, with an explicit "who sees it" choice (admins only, or everyone) before it goes live.

**Validated deploy (dry run) before commit**
- Fetched: Trailhead "Test and Deploy Changes" (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/org-development-model/test-and-deploy-changes, accessed 2026-10-02).
  - "A validated deploy enables you to verify the results of tests that would be executed in a deployment, but doesn't commit any changes."
  - "A successful validation means that all the Apex tests have passed and the tests cover at least 75% of the code being deployed." The validation returns a job ID used for a later "quick deploy".
  - Source of truth for the release "now lives in their GitHub repo"; deploy with `sf project deploy start` and a `package.xml` manifest.
- Metis transfer: a "validate only" run of a framework or pack import that executes all checks (missing approver roles, unreachable stages, gates without quorum) and returns a report and an ID that can later be applied unchanged.

**Post-install scripts (InstallHandler)** [Unverified - confirm before applying]
- Search summary only (developer.salesforce.com returned HTTP 403): a managed package can name one Apex class implementing `InstallHandler`; it runs after install or upgrade and can "populate custom settings, create sample data, send an email to the installer, notify an external system"; if the script fails, the install fails. Source pages: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexref.meta/apexref/apex_install_handler.htm and https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg2_dev.meta/pkg2_dev/apex_post_install_script_intro.htm (not opened).
- Metis transfer: a pack can carry a post-install step (create sample portfolio, seed option lists, assign default roles) that runs once, idempotently, with a clear failure report.

**Industry clouds (prebuilt data model)**
- Fetched: Trailhead "Explore Unified Data Models for Financial Services Success" (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/fsc_data_model/fsc_data_model_unit_1, accessed 2026-10-02): "Agentforce Financial Services adds to that foundation with its Financial Account Data Model, which includes objects you need to track financial accounts, transactions, assets, and more." And: "If you're a new Agentforce Financial Services user, we recommend that you use standard features and objects."
- Metis transfer: industry packs (for example pharma stage-gate, capital projects, IT portfolio) should extend one standard core model rather than invent per-pack objects, so reports and upgrades keep working.

**Salesforce Go (guided setup hub, one-click solutions)**
- Fetched: Trailhead "Explore the Salesforce Go Interface for Admins" (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/sales-cloud-go-quick-look/streamline-your-sales-setup-with-sales-cloud-go, accessed 2026-10-02): "The Initial Setup tab offers setup cards that are especially useful for new organizations, allowing you to complete first-time setup activities in one place"; users can "turn on and configure all of these components with just a few clicks"; "automating configuration tasks that would otherwise take hours" (no number given).
- Fetched: Trailhead "Streamline Your Service Implementation with Salesforce Go" (https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/service_lex/service_lex_connect, accessed 2026-10-02): "it aggregates the most critical setup tasks, checklists, and feature toggles into a single, guided experience."
- Fetched, partner source: Vantage Point blog, David Cockrum, 2026-05-23 (https://vantagepoint.io/blog/sf/salesforce-go-guided-setup-platform-implementation-guide?hs_amp=true): Jumpstart solutions are "pre-configured packages of metadata and sample data that can be installed with a single click"; "An out-of-the-box flow loads sample data so admins can immediately see the feature in action"; claim "Implementation time: weeks" to "minutes" (partner claim, method not stated). Household Jumpstart example configures Households, Financial Accounts, Life Events, Interaction Summaries, Record Rollups in one click.
- Metis transfer: a single setup hub with cards, where each card installs a small pack (configuration plus sample data) and shows the result immediately.

### 4.2 ServiceNow: update sets, Store apps, SPM setup hub

**Update sets: capture, retrieve, preview, commit, back out** (official docs fetched, Washington DC release bundle)
- Definition, fetched (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/washingtondc-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/concept/system-update-sets.html): "An update set is a group of configuration changes that can be moved from one instance to another."
- Preview, fetched (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/washingtondc-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/task/t_PreviewARemoteUpdateSet.html):
  - "Previewing checks a retrieved update set against the local instance to find issues."
  - Compares "the latest local object version with the update set, marking differences with colors" (green added, yellow changed, red deleted).
  - Collision: "a change in the update set is older than a change to the same object on the local instance."
  - "Resolve all problems before committing the update set."
- Commit, fetched (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/washingtondc-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/task/t_CommitAnUpdateSet.html): "You can't commit an update set until all problems are resolved." After commit, review the "Commit log" for unsafe edit warnings and errors.
- Back out, fetched (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/washingtondc-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/task/t_BackOutUpdateSet.html):
  - Per problem, choose "Decide to Keep Current" or "Decide to Use Previous".
  - "Backing out an update set adds delete updates to your current set. If you commit, back out, and reapply a remote update set, preview errors occur due to recent deletions causing collisions."
  - "Some changes caused by a back-out can result in data loss."
  - "Don't back out the Default update set. This action can damage the configuration of the instance."
  - Backing out a set in a batch also backs out its children.
- Transfer methods, fetched (https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/washingtondc-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/reference/update-set-transfers.html): ReleaseOps, update source between instances, or "unload an update set as an XML file and then transfer it to another instance."
- Practitioner evidence, fetched (ServiceNow Community, vendor-hosted, user-authored):
  - Paul Morris, 2023-06-13 (https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-articles/everything-you-need-to-know-about-using-update-sets/ta-p/2586419): "Not everything is captured in update sets (only tables that extend sys_metadata or have the update_sync attribute)"; "Backing out update sets rarely works, often failing halfway through, leaving you even more of a mess to clean up"; recommends fix-forward plans.
  - Mayur Shardul, 2024-10-16 (https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-articles/types-of-errors-causes-amp-solutions-in-update-set/ta-p/3075060): preview error types "Missing object", "Collision", "Uncommitted update", "Warning" (data loss, such as deleting a table); actions include "Accept remote update" and "Skip remote update".
- Metis transfer: treat a lifecycle framework change like an update set: retrieve, preview with per-object diff and typed problems (collision with a local edit, missing approver group, data-loss warning when a stage that holds projects is removed), block publish until every problem has a decision, keep a commit log. Prefer fix-forward (publish a new version) over back-out, because back-out is the least reliable step even on a mature platform.

**Store apps and scoped apps** [Unverified - confirm before applying]
- Search summary only (London-release doc URL now redirects to the docs home page): apps from the ServiceNow Store or the company application repository are installed from the Application Manager; if required plugins are missing, install is blocked and the missing plugins are listed in a "Dependency Checklist". Old URL: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/london-application-development/page/build/applications/task/t_InstallApplications.html (redirected, not opened).
- Metis transfer: a pack declares its dependencies (for example "requires the Finance module" or "requires currency set") and the installer lists unmet ones before anything is written.

**SPM (Strategic Portfolio Management) setup hub and pre-built playbooks** (closest PPM analogue)
- Fetched: "Welcome to Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) Quick Start Guide", Vinitha Chukkala (ServiceNow employee), published 2024-07-16, last updated 2026-08-11 (https://www.servicenow.com/community/spm-articles/quick-start-guide-for-strategic-portfolio-management/ta-p/2990613):
  - Setup Hub is "your single location for all SPM administration" with "a guided setup experience with progress tracking built in"; users can revisit steps.
  - Four decisions before setup: organization structure ("Document your business units and department hierarchy"); key users and roles ("Prepare your roster in advance so role assignment in the console is a quick step rather than a discovery exercise"); fiscal settings ("fiscal calendar type...funding frequency...system currency", noting "fiscal calendar type is configured once and cannot be changed"); governance ("your demand intake process and approval stages", "project approval workflow and status report cadence").
  - "SPM includes pre-built demand and project playbooks"; "know what you want to keep versus customize before you begin."
- Metis transfer: Metis needs the same short pre-setup decision list (org tree, roster, fiscal calendar and currency, gate approvals and reporting cadence) that can be filled in by several people before the 30-minute session, and must flag the few irreversible settings (fiscal calendar type) so everything else can default and change later.

### 4.3 Atlassian: templates, shared configuration, configuration deploy apps

**Create a project that shares another project's configuration**
- Fetched: "Create and edit a service project", last modified 2023-04-28 (https://confluence.atlassian.com/servicedeskcloud/create-and-edit-a-service-project-1097175899.html):
  - "Only Jira admins can create projects with a shared configuration." Not on the Free plan; "applies only to company-managed projects."
  - Shared: "issue types", "workflows", "screens", "fields", "permissions", "notifications"; for Jira Service Management also "Queues", "Reports", "Request types", "SLAs", "Components", language support.
  - Not shared: portal settings, customer notifications, knowledge base, automation and forms.
  - "If a change is made to one of the projects' configurations, that change affects all the projects that share that configuration."
- Search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying]: the REST API has no equivalent of "share settings" (Atlassian issue JRACLOUD-45929); a bug JRACLOUD-92222 gives the new project the type of the shared project rather than the template.
- Metis transfer: "new workspace like workspace X" (shared or copied framework) is a cheap setup path for the second and later business units; Metis must make the shared versus copied choice explicit because shared changes ripple to every sharer.

**Templates by team type**
- Fetched: Jira templates gallery (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/templates, accessed 2026-10-02): 10 categories (Software development, Marketing, Design, Sales, Operations, Service management, Human resources, Legal, IT Operations, Finance); no counts shown.
- Fetched: HR service management template page (https://www.atlassian.com/software/jira/templates/hr-service-management): "out-of-the-box request types and workflows for processes such as employee onboarding and offboarding, change requests, and general questions for HR."
- Search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying]: the support article "About Jira Service Management space templates" (https://support.atlassian.com/jira-service-management-cloud/docs/what-are-the-project-templates/) lists IT, HR, Facilities, Legal, General, Customer, Finance, Marketing, Analytics, Sales and Design service management templates plus a blank space; the fetch returned only the navigation index.
- Metis transfer: name packs by team or industry type and state exactly what each contains (stages, gates, artifacts, option lists, roles).

**Configuration Manager for Jira Cloud (Appfire, Marketplace app)**
- Fetched: overview, last updated "August 7" (year not shown) (https://appfire.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CMJC/pages/193725041): snapshots "capture a project's configuration at a specific point in time, allowing you to review the proposed changes, analyze their impact on the destination site, and resolve potential conflicts before deployment"; capabilities include promote between environments, "standardize configurations across multiple sites", "create projects from templates"; three steps: create snapshot, review and analyze, deploy.
- Fetched: "Deploy configuration changes from Jira Cloud to Cloud" (https://appfire.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CMJC/pages/258053021/Deploy+configuration+changes+from+Jira+Cloud+to+Cloud, page showed "Last updated 1 day ago" on 2026-10-02): setup "Prepare a temporary Jira Cloud site or Atlassian sandbox that mirrors the destination site"; baseline, modify, "Conduct UAT with stakeholders", deploy snapshot; "CMJ Cloud is built to protect the integrity of the destination Jira Cloud site by blocking breaking changes"; analysis separates warnings from blocking errors.
- Metis transfer: a framework snapshot that can be exported from a "design" workspace and deployed to another workspace or tenant with an impact analysis (warnings versus blocking errors). This is also the mechanism a consultancy partner needs to ship a pack.

- Fetched: "Control Center Global Updates: Dashboards" (https://help.smartsheet.com/articles/2479391-control-center-global-updates-dashboards): roll template changes "out across all existing projects"; advice to "run the update on one project and check the results before you run it on all your projects"; "You can't reverse the changes."
- Fetched: "Control Center: Enhanced global updates overview" (https://help.smartsheet.com/articles/2483474-control-center-enhanced-global-updates-overview): add, remove and update "sheets (including columns and cross-sheet formulas), forms, reports, and dashboards"; Preview "creates a temporary copy of that project workspace that matches the template", deleted automatically; on Publish "all active projects sync to it"; eligibility includes blueprints whose projects were created after December 4, 2024, single-tier, no optional templates; warning that it overwrites project-level customizations of template columns (dropdown options, formulas).
- Metis transfer: the closest PPM analogue for "publish framework version 2 to running projects": preview on a temporary copy of one real project, then publish to all, with an explicit policy for local overrides (Smartsheet overwrites them; Metis should show them in the preview and let the admin keep or replace).

**Broadcom Clarity blueprints (PPM)**
- Fetched: Clarity 16.2.1 TechDocs "Configure Blueprints for Projects" (https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/ca-enterprise-software/business-management/clarity-project-and-portfolio-management-ppm-on-premise/16-2-1/using/Getting-Started-with-Clarity-Administration/Getting-Started-with-Blueprints-Grid/new-user-experience-configure-blueprints-for-projects-and-investments.html): the Standard Project blueprint cannot be modified, but "you can make a copy and then edit your copy"; "all existing templates are associated with the Standard Project blueprint by default"; after publishing, "all projects that are associated with the blueprint display the latest layout"; limits "50 modules, 25 visuals, and 200 attributes for the project blueprint."
- Metis transfer: ship a locked "standard" framework that customers copy and edit, never modify in place, so vendor upgrades to the standard stay possible.

### 4.5 Vendor and consultancy implementation packs

**Oracle NetSuite SuiteSuccess**
- Fetched: Oracle NetSuite help "SuiteSuccess" (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_1511800348.html, accessed 2026-10-02): "With SuiteSuccess, you'll get predefined components based on leading practices, specific to your company's industry and your users' roles." Preconfigured components: business processes via SuiteApps, center tabs, chart of accounts, dashboards, enabled features, forms, KPI scorecards, modules, predefined preferences, reports, roles, saved searches. Industries listed on that page: Apparel, Footwear and Accessories; Financials; Food and Beverage; Health and Beauty; Non-Profit; Retail and Hospitality; Software; Wholesale Distribution.
- Search summary only [Unverified - confirm before applying]: go-live "in 100 days or less" (netsuite.com article, HTTP 403 on fetch); "as little as 45 days" (2019 Oracle press release); "3,000 hours" of built-in practices; partner Terillium reports an average of 100 to 140 days versus about nine months for traditional approaches. All are vendor or partner claims without stated method.
- Metis transfer: an industry pack is more than a workflow; it should include roles, dashboards, KPIs, option lists and saved views, so the first login already looks like the customer's industry.

**Workday Launch**
- Fetched: Workday "Deployment and Launch" (https://www.workday.com/en-us/services/deployment.html, accessed 2026-10-02): Launch Express "ten-to-twenty plus-week time frame", "Fixed-fee packages", "Start fast with a preconfigured environment", "Prescribed scope and timeline"; Launch Flex "as few as twenty-seven weeks" with "Prescribed packaging and pricing options". Vendor claim, method not stated.
- Fetched (PDF read): Workday Launch UK datasheet, © 2018, code 20170627LAUNCH-ENUK (https://www.workday.com/content/dam/web/uk/documents/datasheets/datasheet-launch-uk.pdf): "Using common artefacts from past medium enterprise deployments, this standard, preconfigured package is the most effective, lowest-risk way to get you live in four to six months"; "You will be presented with a preconfigured tenant based on what we learned from the discovery process and medium enterprise best practices"; "Since we preload your data into the tenant, you'll be able to see your data in action and make critical decisions with confidence from the start. You can then expand and refine the preconfigured prototype"; "customer satisfaction rating of over 95 per cent" (vendor claim, method not stated).
- Fetched (PDF read): "Five Strategies for a Successful Launch Deployment", © 2023, code 20230313-gbr-launch-guide-gl-ENBX (https://forms.workday.com/content/dam/web/be/documents/other/gbr-launch-guide-gl-en-BE.pdf): "Realise value 42% faster with Workday Launch" (vendor claim, method not stated in the document); "With more than 6,000 deployments under our belt"; "Preconfigured packages get you live in 4 to 6 months... for Workday Financial Management clients, that time frame can shrink to as few as 10 to 12 weeks"; "we preload your data, not dummy data, so you can see it in action" (dash in original replaced by commas); customer quote, City of Port Orange ERP project manager: "right after we signed the contract, we got our first tenant and started seeing samples of our own data in it so we could take an agile, iterative approach to our configuration"; Midtown Athletics went live "in just five months".

### 4.6 Configuration as code: plan, apply, drift

**Terraform plan and apply semantics**
- Fetched: HashiCorp "terraform plan" (https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/plan, accessed 2026-10-02): plan "Reads the current state of any already-existing remote objects", "Compares the current configuration to the prior state", "Proposes a set of change actions"; "The plan command alone does not actually carry out the proposed changes." A saved plan (`-out=FILE`) contains "your full configuration, all of the values associated with planned changes", so apply executes exactly what was reviewed.
- Fetched: HCP Terraform "Health assessments" (https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/health, accessed 2026-10-02): "Drift detection helps you identify situations where your actual infrastructure no longer matches the configuration defined in Terraform"; assessments run speculative plans on a schedule (example: 24-hour cadence measured from the last apply or assessment); on drift, either "Queue a new plan and apply the changes to revert" or update the configuration to accept the drift.
- Metis transfer: "plan" is the right mental model for publishing a framework: show created, changed and removed stages, gates and rules before anything changes, and apply exactly the reviewed plan.

**Okta (vendor-documented Terraform)**
- Fetched: Okta "Terraform overview" (https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/terraform-overview/main/, no date shown): benefits "Apply oversight and auditing to changes in your orgs", "Implement best practices for operations, such as source control and automated deployment"; plan "Generates a preview of the resources that Terraform creates, changes, and removes"; "Okta recommends managing a type of object in your org using either Terraform or the Admin Console. Managing the same objects... with multiple methods can introduce synchronization issues and increases the risk of errors."
- Fetched: Okta "Import existing Okta objects into Terraform" (https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/terraform-import-existing-resources/main/): add an import block, then "Continue to run terraform plan and make minor changes until there are no changed values in the output"; "Skipping this step can cause unexpected changes that may reduce the reliability and security of your org"; `terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf` generates configuration from existing objects.
- Fetched: Okta "Optimize Terraform access to Okta APIs" (https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/terraform-design-rate-limits/main/): save a plan with `-out` and apply it later; run without refresh "only if admins and other apps aren't managing your org. Otherwise, configuration drift can occur and cause errors."
- Fetched: GitHub repo okta/terraform-provider-okta (https://github.com/okta/terraform-provider-okta): "A Terraform provider to manage Okta resources... users, groups, applications, and other Okta objects", maintained by Okta.
- Metis transfer: if Metis offers configuration as code, it must also offer "export current configuration to code" (generate config) and must say per object type whether code or UI is the owner, otherwise UI edits and code fight.

**Other vendor-maintained Terraform providers (existence check)**
- Fetched GitHub repos (accessed 2026-10-02): PagerDuty/terraform-provider-pagerduty (maintained by PagerDuty; users, teams, services, escalation policies, schedules); DataDog/terraform-provider-datadog (official DataDog org); integrations/terraform-provider-github ("repositories, teams, branch protections, actions secrets/variables, organization settings, rulesets, deploy keys, webhooks").
- Note: registry.terraform.io pages render client-side and returned no content to WebFetch.

**Auth0 Deploy CLI (native SaaS configuration as code)**
- Fetched: https://auth0.com/docs/deploy-monitor/deploy-cli-tool (accessed 2026-10-02): "a tool that helps you manage your Auth0 tenant configuration" via export and import in YAML or directory (JSON) format; designed "from feature branch all the way to production"; "Keyword Replacement" for environment-specific values; "This tool can be destructive to your Auth0 tenant", so deletions require `AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE` to be enabled.
- Metis transfer: an export and import format with environment keywords (for example currency, calendar, approver group names) lets one pack serve many workspaces; deletes must be opt-in.

**Microsoft365DSC (export a live tenant to code, detect drift)**
- Fetched: https://microsoft365dsc.com/ (accessed 2026-10-02): "take snapshots of the current configuration of any existing Microsoft 365 tenant"; drift detection that can "automatically detect a drift"; compare environments; reports; "an Open-Source initiative hosted on GitHub, led by Microsoft engineers and maintained by the community."

**Salto (SaaS configuration management for business apps)**
- Fetched: Salto blog, Gil Hoffer, 2024-03-21 (https://www.salto.io/blog-posts/terraform-and-salto-two-paths-to-effective-okta-configuration-management), vendor source: "fetch" "automatically generates and updates the code representation of a service from its current implementation"; contrasts Terraform's assumption that changes are "always done using code and never directly in the service itself"; supports "tenant-to-tenant compare and deploy", "change-based deployments" and "restore"; does not require admins to learn the code representation.
- Metis transfer: most PPM admins will configure in the UI; a "fetch to readable snapshot, compare, deploy" model (Salto, CMJ) fits them better than code-first Terraform, while still giving partners a file they can version.

### 4.7 YAML or JSON configuration import and export in SaaS products

- Grafana provisioning, fetched (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/provisioning/, accessed 2026-10-02): "You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural"; YAML for data sources, dashboards, alerting; with `allowUiUpdates` enabled, UI edits save but "If you save a provisioned dashboard in the UI and then later update the provisioning source, Grafana always overwrites the database dashboard with the one from the provisioning file"; with it disabled, UI save of a provisioned dashboard is blocked.
- Backstage descriptor format, fetched (https://backstage.io/docs/features/software-catalog/descriptor-format): recommended file `catalog-info.yaml`; envelope `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`; YAML for humans and JSON in the API "maintain identical structure and meaning"; entities live in source control; invalid entities are rejected at registration.
- Port, fetched glossary (https://docs.port.io/glossary): a blueprint is "Port's schema definition for a catalog type... closer to a class definition in object-oriented programming"; an entity is "a concrete instance of a blueprint"; the glossary mentions a Port Terraform provider. The dedicated blueprint setup page URL returned HTTP 404.
- GitLab instance template repository, fetched (https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/settings/instance_template_repository/): an administrator picks a project as "the instance-wide collection of file templates" (Dockerfiles, .gitignore, .gitlab-ci.yml, LICENSE, issue and merge request templates), exposed to all users; Premium and Ultimate tiers.
- Retool Source Control, fetched (https://docs.retool.com/source-control): "Manage changes to Retool apps using SCM providers and version control"; changes to apps, workflows, resources and themes go through pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, AWS CodeCommit, Bitbucket or Azure Repos. File format details not in the fetched excerpt.
- Postman, fetched (https://learning.postman.com/docs/getting-started/importing-and-exporting/exporting-data/): export collections, environments and globals "as JSON files" and "import back into any Postman instance"; bulk export of all workspaces via account settings.
- Metis transfer: one documented, versioned schema (YAML for humans, JSON for API, same structure) for workspace profile, option lists, frameworks and portfolio tree; validation on import with typed errors; an "owned by file" flag that locks UI edits (Grafana) for regulated frameworks.

Evidence gap: no independent study (non-vendor, with stated method) was found that measures time-to-value or setup time with versus without configuration packs or templates. All time savings above are vendor or partner claims.

**Top transferable ideas for Metis (topic 4)**
1. Versioned framework packs with plan, preview and publish. Ship lifecycle frameworks, deliverable process frameworks, option lists and workspace profile defaults as immutable, numbered packs (vendor, partner or customer authored, reviewed before listing). Installing or upgrading a pack produces a plan: every stage, gate, approver rule and artifact that will be created, changed or removed, typed problems (collision with a local edit, missing approver role, data-loss warning for a stage holding live projects), and publish is blocked until each problem has a decision. Apply exactly the reviewed plan, keep a commit log, prefer fix-forward over back-out, and preview a version-2 rollout on a temporary copy of one real project before syncing all projects. Sources: Salesforce packages, ServiceNow update sets, Terraform plan, CMJ, Smartsheet enhanced global updates, Clarity blueprints.
2. Preconfigured workspace loaded with the customer's own portfolio, reviewed fit-to-standard. Start the 30-minute session from an industry pack that is already running, import the customer's existing project list into it immediately, and walk the admin through a short questionnaire that records only deltas; collect the few irreversible decisions (fiscal calendar type, currency, org tree) up front from the right people, and default everything else. Sources: Workday Launch preloaded data, SAP starter system and fit-to-standard, ServiceNow SPM pre-setup decisions, Salesforce Go Jumpstart sample data, NetSuite SuiteSuccess roles and dashboards.

## 5. Progressive configuration

### 5.1 Recommendations computed from the tenant's own configuration or usage

**5.1.1 Microsoft Entra recommendations** [F]
- What it does: a recommendations list in the Entra admin center that is computed per tenant and shows only the items that apply.
- Mechanics, quoted: "On a daily basis, Microsoft Entra ID analyzes the configuration of your tenant. During this analysis, Microsoft Entra ID compares the configuration of your tenant with security best practices and recommendation data." "Microsoft Entra only displays the recommendations that apply to your tenant." Each recommendation has "a description, a summary of the value of addressing the recommendation, and a step-by-step action plan" plus impacted resources. A preview feature "sends emails to a predetermined set of roles for each recommendation" (for example, application items go to the Application Administrator role).
- Usage-based examples in the table: "Remove unused applications", "Remove unused credentials from applications", "Review inactive users with Access Reviews".
- The 90-day inactivity threshold for "Remove unused applications" was seen only in a search summary [S] [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/overview-recommendations (ms.date 2026-04-28).
- Metis transfer: a daily "workspace health" evaluation that lists only the setup items that apply (for example a gate with no approver, a quorum larger than the approver pool, an option list nobody uses) and routes each item by email to the role that owns it.

**5.1.2 Microsoft Secure Score recommended actions** [F]
- What it does: a ranked list of configuration actions with a score.
- Mechanics, quoted: "Ranking is based on the number of points left to achieve, implementation difficulty, user impact, and complexity." Statuses: "to address, planned, risk accepted, resolved through third party, resolved through alternate mitigation, and completed". "Risk accepted" gives no points; "Resolved through third party" gives the points. Each action has a deep link ("Manage in Microsoft Defender XDR"), a "Share" link (email, Teams, Planner), notes, tags, a "User impact" and "Users affected" section and prerequisites. Points take "between 24-48 hours" to show.
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/microsoft-secure-score-improvement-actions (ms.date 2025-04-28, updated_at 2026-05-03).
- Metis transfer: setup items carry honest closing states ("not applicable", "handled elsewhere", "accepted risk") so a 30-minute setup can end with a complete list rather than a forced wizard; a share link per item lets the admin hand one item to a colleague.

**5.1.3 Okta HealthInsight** [F for the task table; S for the tab behaviour]
- What it does: security tasks for the org, each with a security impact and an end-user impact rating.
- Quoted examples: limit super admin roles (security Critical, end-user None) "To ensure that org admins aren't assigned more permissions than necessary"; enforce limited session lifetime (High, Moderate); disable weaker MFA factors (High, High).
- Incomplete and Complete tabs, dismiss for tasks that do not apply, and deep links to the setting: seen in search summary only [S] [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Source: https://help.okta.com/en-us/content/topics/security/healthinsight/healthinsight-security-task-recomendations.htm (accessed 2026-10-02).
- Metis transfer: rate every recommended governance setting on two axes, governance value and burden on project teams, so admins see the trade-off.

**5.1.4 Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness: "Suggested candidate for Copilot"** [F]
- What it does: flags which unlicensed users to license first, from observed app usage.
- Mechanics, quoted: "Each week, the feature flags the top 25% of nonlicensed users within an organization." It uses "usage metrics for the preceding 28-day period"; "several of the inputs to the suggestion model are also shown"; "This data isn't intended to be used to evaluate employee performance." Recommended action cards include "assigning available Copilot licenses".
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/microsoft-365-copilot-readiness (ms.date 2026-04-03).
- Metis transfer: usage-driven suggestions with visible inputs, for example "these 6 projects already track budgets in attachments, enable the budget module for them".

**5.1.5 Datadog Monitor Templates (formerly Recommended Monitors)** [F]
- Mechanics, quoted: "If you have fewer than 10 monitors, Datadog automatically recommends a list of Integration-Monitor Templates based on your installed integrations."
- Source: https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/templates/ (accessed 2026-10-02).
- 2020 blog detail that each recommended monitor ships with a default query, thresholds and tags: [S] [Unverified - confirm before applying] (https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/datadog-recommended-monitors/).
- Metis transfer: show starter-pack recommendations only while the workspace is sparse (a threshold), and base them on what has been connected or imported.

**5.1.6 GitHub Actions CI workflow suggestions** [F]
- Mechanics, quoted: "When you set up CI in your repository, GitHub analyzes the code in your repository and recommends CI workflows based on the language and framework in your repository."

### 5.2 Opinionated defaults that stay editable

**5.2.1 Linear default workflow** [F]
- Quoted default: "Backlog > Todo > In Progress > Done > Canceled". Statuses are edited in "Settings -> Teams -> Issue statuses"; "Teams can reorder statuses within each status category, but the categories themselves stay in a fixed order."
- Source: https://linear.app/docs/configuring-workflows (accessed 2026-10-02).
- Metis transfer: ship a default lifecycle with fixed stage categories (for example idea, define, deliver, close) whose names, gates and artifacts are editable, so reporting stays comparable across workspaces.

### 5.3 Just-in-time setup at the point of need

**5.3.1 Notion link previews** [F]
- Quoted: "The first time that you paste a link from one of these platforms, you'll see a button that asks you to connect to the app." Supported apps include GitHub, Jira, Slack, Asana, Trello, Linear, Figma, Box, ClickUp and Zendesk.
- Source: https://www.notion.com/help/link-previews (accessed 2026-10-02).

**5.3.2 Stripe: sandbox first, verification at go-live** [F]
- Quoted: "After creating a Stripe account, you can test Stripe services in a sandbox." "To use a service in live mode, verify your business and complete its activation requirements." And: "After activating a Stripe service on a live account, you can't change the business origin country."
- Source: https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/activate (accessed 2026-10-02).
- Metis transfer: let the customer build the workspace in a draft state; require approvers, quorum and mandatory artifacts only at "publish framework"; flag the few irreversible choices explicitly.

**5.3.3 QuickBooks Online multicurrency (counter-example: an irreversible deferred setting)** [F]
- Quoted: "Once Multicurrency is on, you can't turn it off again, or change your home currency." Reason: "currency conversion information will have to be accounted for in the system moving forward."

- Metis transfer: classify every setup field as reversible or irreversible; defer only reversible ones; for irreversible ones (likely the workspace base currency once budgets exist) either ask once with a clear warning or engineer them to be reversible.

**5.3.4 HubSpot progressive fields (progressive profiling)** [F]
- Quoted: "if the contact filling out your form already has a value for a specific field, you can use progressive fields to set another field to appear in its place." Limitation: "Progressive fields are not supported in the updated form editor."
- Source: https://knowledge.hubspot.com/forms/use-progressive-fields-in-forms (accessed 2026-10-02).
- Metis transfer: collect the missing workspace profile items one or two at a time at natural moments (first budget, first report) instead of a long upfront form.

**5.3.5 Salesforce Starter: goals survey drives a snoozable checklist** [F, third-party review]
- Quoted from a hands-on review: users complete "a brief survey about your business goals", then see "Explore Cards, which are shortcuts to recommended tools based on your survey responses"; each card "launches a guided walk-through with on-page prompts and a sidebar checklist you can move, minimize, or snooze"; users can "mark tasks complete or bookmark them for later".
- Source: Alison Barretta, Yahoo Tech, https://tech.yahoo.com/business/articles/salesforce-starter-suite-100000136.html (updated 2025-10-13).

**5.3.6 Salesforce Free Suite** [F]
- Quoted: "Set up in minutes without needing an IT team or specialists"; Guided Checklist with "step-by-step guidance to set up your CRM in minutes". Vendor claim, method not stated.
- Source: https://www.salesforce.com/crm/free-crm/ (accessed 2026-10-02).

### 5.4 Empty states that teach, and disclosure depth

**5.4.1 NN/g, "Designing Empty States in Complex Applications: 3 Guidelines"** [F]
- Kate Kaplan, 2021-09-19. Empty states are containers "for which content does not yet exist or otherwise cannot be displayed" and are "quite common during onboarding and initial usage". Guidelines: communicate system status, provide learning cues ("pull revelations" that "show up only when the user interacts with the corresponding UI element"), provide direct pathways for key tasks. Example: Loggly offers "adding external log sources or populating demo data".
- Source: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/ (2021-09-19).
- Evidence quality: expert guidance from a UX research firm, no quantitative study in the article text seen.

**5.4.2 NN/g, "Onboarding Tutorials vs. Contextual Help"** [F]
- Page Laubheimer, 2023-02-12. Push revelations (tutorials) are "typically pushy, devoid of context, and intrusive"; the article states tutorials "don't result in better task performance" and users "frequently skip them"; cites the paradox of the active user. Recommends contextual help triggered "when the user would benefit from that information at that moment".
- Source: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/onboarding-tutorials/ (2023-02-12).
- Evidence quality: expert synthesis; the underlying studies were not visible in the fetched text, so treat as guidance, not measurement.
- Metis transfer: supports the product owner's "no slide tours" constraint; teach inside empty states and at first use.

**5.4.3 NN/g, "Progressive Disclosure"** [F]
- Jakob Nielsen, 2006-12-03. "designs that go beyond 2 disclosure levels typically have low usability because users often get lost when moving between the levels." Staged disclosure (wizards) works when steps are independent and becomes problematic when "steps are interdependent and users must alternate between them."
- Source: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/ (2006-12-03).
- Metis transfer: a lifecycle framework is interdependent (gates reference stages, approvers, artifacts and rules), so it fits a single canvas with live validation better than a linear wizard.

**5.4.4 IBM Carbon Design System, empty states pattern** [F]
- Three types: no data (first use), user action, error management. "Starter content can provide the opportunity for users to dive in and learn about primary features and functions with sample data." "Pre-configured kits and workflows" offer "a fast path to getting started". "As a general rule, don't lead the user into a dead end."
- Source: https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/empty-states-pattern/ (accessed 2026-10-02).

**5.4.5 Atlassian Design System, empty state** [F]
- Distinguishes an empty state ("when someone clears a screen or finishes a piece of work") from a blank slate ("people have never come across or tried a new feature before"). Body copy should "Include the reason for the empty state and where they can go next"; CTAs use imperative verbs such as "Create".
- Source: https://atlassian.design/foundations/content/designing-messages/empty-state (accessed 2026-10-02).

### 5.5 Sample data that can be removed

**5.5.1 Pipedrive sample data** [F]
- Quoted: "Sample data is a pre-configured set of sample records and information used to demonstrate a system's features and functionality." Each sample record starts with "[Sample]"; status visible under the Quick help icon; only global admins can remove it, from Quick help, the import page or Insights.
- Source: https://support.pipedrive.com/en/article/sample-data (last updated 2026-09-03).
- Metis transfer: a demo portfolio labelled [Sample], excluded from real reporting, removable by the workspace admin in one action.

## 6. Concierge and implementation-in-a-day offers

Summary: no verified vendor offers a literal "implementation in a day" for enterprise governance or PPM software. The fastest verified claims: days to 2 weeks (Ramp, spend management, pilot group), 30 days (Planview planning package via FastTrack; Ramp full implementation), 4 weeks (Capture SmartStart for ServiceNow SPM, a partner package), 60 business days (Workday GO). All timing numbers below are vendor or partner claims unless stated otherwise.

### 6.3 Outcomes: onboarding, time to value and retention

**6.3.1 TSIA, "The Power of Customer Success in Reducing Churn"** [F]
- Quoted: "Accounts with a CSM have a churn rate less than half that of accounts without one." CSM involvement during onboarding is called critical for adoption and renewals.
- Source: https://www.tsia.com/research/reducing-churn-customer-success-insights (2024-09-17). Quality: industry association survey (TSIA Intelligence), sample size not stated in the public excerpt, correlational.

**6.3.2 TSIA, "Customer Onboarding Optimization"** [F]
- Quoted: "A significant barrier to effective onboarding is customers' lack of time and resources, impacting their ability to engage fully." No public numbers.
- Source: https://www.tsia.com/research/customer-onboarding-optimization-as-a-catalyst (2025-06-03).
- Metis transfer: the binding constraint is customer time, which argues for distributing setup items to owners and for vendor-side import.

**6.3.3 Drata case at Gainsight Pulse 2026, "Cutting Time-to-Value by 55%"** [F]
- Kat Kenny, Director of Digital Customer Success, Drata (a compliance SaaS with heavy setup). In-app checklist program (Chameleon, Amplitude, data warehouse). Reported: time to value from 144 to 66 days on average (55%); "Five times the amount of customers who achieved value in the first 30 days"; emerging-segment admin retention 40.8% to 68.5%; customers reaching the "value stage" renewed at 92%. Caveat quoted: "I've only got two months worth of renewal data at this point."
- Source: https://pulselibrary.gainsight.com/video/cutting-time-to-value-by-55-the-digital-onboarding-playbook/ (Pulse 2026; accessed 2026-10-02). Quality: single company, before and after, self-reported, short renewal window, no control group.

**6.3.4 Third-party statistics seen and not used** [S]
- Optifai (939 companies), SaaSMag, ProfitWell ("43% more likely to churn"), Amplitude (98% of new users churn without a value milestone), and the widely repeated "TSIA: 92% more likely to renew" (which one search summary traces to an Optimizely case of 92% versus 80% renewal). None opened; methods unknown. [Unverified - confirm before applying] Do not cite.
